Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the soil and plant flowers in her garden. One day, she heard a noise coming from the soil. "What's that sound?" she asked her mommy. "It's just a little worm, Lily," her mommy replied.
Lily was eager to see the worm, so she dug deeper into the soil. Suddenly, she heard a loud noise and felt the ground shake. "Mommy, what's happening?" she cried. "It's an earthquake, Lily," her mommy said, trying to calm her down.
The earthquake caused the ground to open up and swallow Lily and her mommy. They were trapped deep in the soil and no one could hear their cries for help. Sadly, they were never found and the flowers in Lily's garden grew without her.

Pip landed on the branch and said, "What is this bitter fruit?" A wise old owl was sitting on another branch nearby and heard Pip's question. The owl said, "That's a persimmon fruit. It's very bitter, but some people like it. Would you like me to explain more about it?"
Pip nodded his head and the owl continued, "Persimmons are fruits that grow on trees. They are orange and round, but they taste very bitter until they are ripe. Then they become sweet and delicious to eat." 
Pip thanked the owl and flew away, feeling grateful for the new knowledge he had learned. He decided to try a persimmon fruit when it was ripe, so he could taste the sweetness for himself.

Tom and Mia were playing on the beach. They liked to find shells and make piles of them. Tom found a big shell that was shiny and had many colors. He was very happy and showed it to Mia.
"Look, Mia, I found a nice shell!" he said.
Mia looked at the shell and frowned. She recognized it. It was the same shell that she had found yesterday and left on her towel. She thought Tom had taken it from her.
"That is my shell, Tom!" she said. "You took it from me!"
Tom was confused and sad. He did not take the shell from Mia. He found it in the sand. He did not want to make Mia angry.
"No, Mia, I did not take your shell. I found it here. See, there are more shells like it." he said and pointed to the sand.
Mia did not believe him. She thought he was lying. She wanted her shell back. She tried to grab it from Tom's hand.
"Give me my shell, Tom! It is mine!" she said.
Tom did not want to give up his shell. He liked it too much. He held it tight and pulled it away from Mia.
"No, Mia, it is my shell! I found it first!" he said.
They both pulled and tugged on the shell. They were both angry and loud. They did not hear their mom calling them.
"Tom! Mia! Come here, please!" their mom said.
She saw them fighting over the shell. She was not happy. She walked over to them and took the shell from their hands.
"Stop it, both of you! What is going on?" she said.
Tom and Mia both tried to explain. They both said the shell was theirs. They both said the other one was wrong.
Their mom looked at the shell. She recognized it too. She had seen it before. She knew who it belonged to.
"Tom, Mia, this shell is not yours. It is not mine. It is not anyone's. It is a shell that belongs to the sea. It is a gift that the sea gives us to enjoy, but not to keep. Do you understand?" she said.
Tom and Mia looked at the shell. They looked at their mom. They looked at each other. They felt sorry for fighting. They nodded.
"Yes, mom, we understand." they said.
Their mom smiled and hugged them. She gave them the shell to hold together.
"Good. Now, why don't you share this nice shell and look for more shells to admire? But remember, when we leave the beach, we have to leave the shells behind. They are not ours to take. They are the sea's to give." she said.
Tom and Mia agreed. They thanked their mom and said sorry to each other. They held the shell and looked at its colors. They felt happy and peaceful. They went back to playing on the beach. They found more shells and made piles of them. They shared them and admired them. They did not fight over them. They had fun.

Tom was a cat who liked to play outside. He ran, jumped and chased birds and mice. He did not like to take baths or brush his fur. He thought he looked fine with his dirty, tangled coat.
One day, it was very cold and windy. Tom wanted to find a warm place to sleep. He saw a big house with a nice garden. He sneaked in through a hole in the fence. He saw a dog house with a soft blanket inside. He thought it was perfect for him.
He crawled into the dog house and curled up on the blanket. He felt cozy and happy. He did not know that the dog house belonged to Rex, a big, friendly dog who lived in the house.
Soon, Rex came back from his walk with his owner. He smelled a strange scent in his dog house. He barked and ran to see who was there. He saw Tom, the dirty cat, sleeping on his blanket. He was angry and scared.
"Who are you? Get out of my house!" Rex growled.
Tom woke up and saw Rex. He was terrified. He hissed and scratched Rex's nose. He tried to run away, but Rex blocked his way.
"Leave me alone! I just wanted to be warm!" Tom cried.
Rex and Tom fought and made a lot of noise. Their owner heard them and came to see what was wrong. He saw Rex and Tom, both hurt and scared. He picked up Tom and took him inside. He cleaned his wounds and gave him some food and water. He also gave him a bath and brushed his fur. He made him look clean and shiny.
He also checked on Rex and gave him a treat and a hug. He told him he was a good boy for protecting his house. He also told him he was sorry for the cat who was lost and cold.
He put Tom in a cage and called the animal shelter. He hoped they would find a good home for him. He felt sorry for him, but he knew he could not keep him. He already had Rex, who was his best friend.
Tom felt warm and full, but also sad and lonely. He wished he had a friend like Rex. He wished he had taken better care of himself. He realized he had been selfish and rude. He shivered in his cage and licked his paw. He hoped someone would love him and teach him how to be a good cat. He learned a hard lesson that day. He learned that being dirty and mean was not fun or smart. He learned that being clean and kind was better for him and others.

"Oh no!" Ben said. "You broke the mushroom! What if it was someone's home? What if a bug lived there?"

"Here you go, worm," Lily said. "This is a new mushroom for you. We hope you are happy. We are sorry for breaking your old mushroom."

"Wow, look at that!" Lily said. "Maybe there is treasure under the ice!"
"Let's find out!" Ben said. He took the hook and tried to break the ice with it. He hit the ice hard, but it did not crack. He hit it again, and again, but nothing happened.
"Be careful, Ben!" Lily said. "You might fall in!"
Ben did not listen. He wanted to find the treasure. He hit the ice harder and harder, until he made a small hole. He looked inside, and saw something shiny. He reached for it with his hook, but he lost his balance. He slipped and fell into the pond.

"Ben, Ben, grab the stick!" she shouted. "I'll pull you out!"
Ben heard Lily's voice. He was very cold and wet. He saw the stick, and grabbed it. Lily pulled him out of the pond. He was shivering and coughing. He dropped the hook, and hugged Lily.
"Thank you, Lily!" he said. "You saved me!"
"I'm sorry, Ben!" Lily said. "I should have been more polite. I should have let you have the hook. It was your treasure."
Ben shook his head. He smiled at Lily. He said, "No, Lily, you are my treasure. The hook was just a hook. It was not worth it. You are my best friend."
They hugged each other, and walked back to their ship. They decided to play pirates another day, when it was warmer and safer. They learned their lesson. They learned to be careful, and to share, and to be polite. They were happy.

"Sure, but be careful. Don't go too close to the water. And don't throw the bread too hard. The swans might get scared," Mom said.
Lily nodded and took a piece of bread from Mom. She walked slowly to the edge of the pond. She saw a swan swimming near her. She smiled and tossed the bread gently to the swan. The swan caught the bread and ate it. It looked happy.
"Thank you, swan!" Lily said.
The swan nodded and swam away. Lily looked for another swan to feed. She saw one that was hidden behind some reeds. It was smaller than the other swans. It looked shy.
"Hello, swan! Do you want some bread?" Lily called.
The hidden swan peeked out from the reeds. It saw Lily and the bread. It wanted the bread, but it was afraid of Lily. It stayed behind the reeds.
"Come on, swan! Don't be scared. I won't hurt you. I just want to be your friend," Lily said.
She threw the bread closer to the hidden swan. The hidden swan saw the bread. It was hungry. It decided to try the bread. It swam out from the reeds and took the bread. It tasted good.
"Thank you, Lily!" The hidden swan said.
Lily was surprised. She didn't know that swans could talk.
"You're welcome, swan! What's your name?" Lily asked.
"My name is End. I'm the last of my family. The other swans left me because I'm different. I can talk, but they can't," End said.
"That's sad, End. But you're not alone. You have me. I'm your friend. And you're not different. You're special," Lily said.
End smiled. He felt happy. He had a friend.
"Thank you, Lily. You're special too. Can I stay with you?" End asked.
"Of course, End. You can stay with me. Come on, let's go to Mom. She'll like you too," Lily said.
She took End's wing and led him to Mom. Ben saw them and was amazed.
"Wow, Lily! You have a talking swan!" Ben said.
"Yes, Ben. This is End. He's my friend. Can he play with us?" Lily said.
"Sure, Lily. He can play with us. Hi, End. I'm Ben. Nice to meet you," Ben said.
"Hi, Ben. Nice to meet you too. You're Lily's brother, right?" End said.
"Yes, I am. You're very smart, End," Ben said.
"Thank you, Ben. You're very kind, Ben," End said.
Mom saw them and was shocked.
"Lily, Ben, what's going on? Who's this swan?" Mom asked.
"Mom, this is End. He's a talking swan. He's my friend. Can he stay with us?" Lily said.
"A talking swan? That's incredible. How did you find him?" Mom asked.
"He was hidden behind some reeds. He was lonely. I gave him some bread. He thanked me. He told me his name. He asked me to be his friend. I said yes. He's very nice, Mom. Please, can he stay with us?" Lily said.
Mom looked at End. He looked at Mom. He nodded.
"Hello, Mom. I'm End. I'm a talking swan. I'm Lily's friend. Can I stay with you?" End said.
Mom was speechless. She didn't know what to say. She looked at Lily and Ben. They looked at Mom. They smiled.
"Please, Mom. Please," they said.
Mom sighed. She smiled too.
"Okay, okay. You can stay with us, End. But only if you promise to be good and not make too much noise. And you have to share the bread with the other swans. Deal?" Mom said.
"Deal, Mom. Thank you, Mom. You're very nice, Mom," End said.
Lily, Ben, and End hugged Mom. They were happy. They had a new friend. A talking swan. His name was End. But his story was just beginning.

From that day on, Lily always made sure to be gentle and balance her blocks just right. She knew that if she did, she could make something amazing too.

Once upon a time there was a lonely volcano. He lived up on a high hill in the middle of a vast, deserted valley. Every night, he would sit on the hilltop and look out into the dark, empty landscape.
The volcano felt terribly lonely and wanted some company. One night, he found a voice. It was arguing with itself. When the volcano asked who was talking, the voice replied that it was only a small bird.
The bird had been flying around all night looking for a place to rest. But the volcano made too much noise so the bird kept on flying. The volcano felt sorry for the bird and invited it to stay with him on the hilltop.
The bird accepted, and the two of them talked until the sun began to rise. The bird told the volcano stories of its travels and the volcano listened. Every night when the sun went down, the volcano and the bird would talk until morning came. 
Then one night, instead of talking, the bird started to complain about how cold and lonely it was up on the hilltop. The volcano felt terrible. He was so sorry to hear the bird complain and wanted to make things better. 
The volcano said to the bird that it could come and stay in the big hollow beneath his peak. The bird accepted, and from then on, the volcano and the bird were friends. The lonely volcano had a companion and was never alone again.

Jenny nodded, feeling tired but happy. She smiled as the boat slowly moved back towards the shore.

Her mother smiled. “That’s lovely! Are you sure you don’t want to keep it?”
The little girl thought for a moment. “No, I will return it to where I found it.”
The next morning the little girl put the coin back in the woods. As she picked it up she noticed a spicy smell, like cooking food.
Suddenly, a voice called out from a nearby bush. “Thank you for returning my coin! You are a kind and honest person.”
The little girl was surprised. Who was talking to her?
As she stepped closer to the bush, she noticed a creature with big eyes and furry ears. He held a spoonful of spicy soup and said, “Here, this is a small thank you for returning my coin.”
The moral of the story is that being kind and honest is always rewarded in the end.

One day, Tim's mom went to the store. She told Tim not to touch the jelly until she came back. But Tim could not wait. He wanted to eat the jelly right away. So he went to the kitchen and tried to get the jelly. But he dropped it, and it fell on the floor. The jelly was spoiled.
Tim was sad. He knew he should have waited for his mom. When his mom came back, she saw the spoiled jelly on the floor. She was not mad. She just hugged Tim and said, "Next time, wait for me, and we will eat the jelly together." Tim learned his lesson and never spoiled the jelly again.

Lily asked her mom, "Can I have some yogurt, please?" Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, but first, you must answer a question. What is something you did today that made you feel proud?"
Lily thought for a moment and said, "I helped my friend when she fell down on the playground. I felt proud because I was a good friend." Her mom smiled and said, "That's wonderful, Lily! You should always be proud of being kind and helpful."
Lily's mom gave her a big spoonful of yogurt. As Lily ate the yogurt, she felt proud of herself. She knew that being kind and helpful was important. From that day on, Lily always tried to be a good friend and help others when they needed it. And every time she ate yogurt, she remembered the lesson her mom taught her.
The moral of the story is: Always be kind and helpful, and you will feel proud of yourself.

From that day on, the wild cat felt like he belonged with the little girl and her family. He found his true home and he was very happy.

It was the yummiest carrot Ted had ever tasted, but something was different about this carrot. As it slipped down his throat, he felt a strange wetness. So Ted hopped over to a nearby pond to take a look. The pond was full of tasty carrot juices!
He quickly hopped back to the carrot patch and found that all the carrots had soaked up all the water from the pond! "Wow!" Ted said, "I'm so lucky I got here quick. I need to be careful next time!"
Ted hopped away with a full tummy, happy to have had such a great adventure. All thanks to that one special carrot!

Finally, a little fish named Zip wanted to come with Tuna. They swam together through the ocean, seeing all kinds of creatures. Tuna was happy to have a friend with him. 
After a while, they got hungry. Tuna remembered he had a can of tuna in his backpack. Zip was confused, but Tuna explained that it was a special kind of fish that humans like to eat. They opened the can and shared the tuna. It was delicious! 
Tuna and Zip continued on their adventure, having fun and seeing new things. Tuna was happy he was patient and waited for a friend to come with him. They swam together, enjoying each other's company.

Sam heard Tim scream. He ran to the garage and saw the spider. He was not scared of spiders. He picked up the sword and chased the spider away. He saved Tim from the spider.
"Thank you, Sam!" Tim said. He hugged Sam and felt sorry. "I am sorry I was mean to you. You are a good friend. Can you please share the sword with me?"
"Of course, Tim!" Sam said. He smiled and handed the sword to Tim. "You are a good friend too. I am grateful you said sorry. Let's play together!"
Tim and Sam learned to share and be kind. They had fun playing with the sword and pretending to be knights. They were happy and proud.

Finally, the old woman asked the wealthy man, "if I can make this chair move backwards, will you agree to change places with me?". The wealthy man thought it was impossible, but he agreed. The old woman then began to move the chair slowly backwards. 
The wealthy man then realised how fortunate he was, and how truly blessed he was to have all the wealth he had. He learned a lesson that day and made sure to never again look down on other people who didn't have as much as him. 
The moral of this story is that being truly wealthy is about what you have in your heart, not just what you have in your pocket.

Suddenly, out from the darkness hopped a small, brown bunny. Alex had never seen him from before. 
"Hi there" the little bunny said. "I was just looking for a pin in the bushes".
Alex was a little disturbed by the bunny, but he was also a little curious. 
"What do you need a pin for?" he asked the bunny.
The little bunny held up a ball of wool and said: "I want to hold the wool together, but I need a pin to do it".
Alex was now feeling less disturbed. He had seen his Mommy using pins when she sewed. So he reached down and picked up a pin from the ground.
He handed it to the bunny who smiled and thanked him. Then he hopped away back into the dark. 
Alex smiled and went back to playing in the garden.

"No, Lila, you can't," Ben said. "It's too big and heavy. And it's silly. Stars can't make wishes."
"Yes, they can," Lila said. "Grandma said so. And it's not silly. It's powerful."
They started to argue. Mom and dad heard them and came to see what was wrong.
"Why are you fighting?" mom asked.
"Lila wants to pack her wish star, but it's too big and heavy. And it's silly," Ben said.
"No, it's not," Lila said. "It's powerful. And I want to bring it."
Mom and dad looked at each other. They knew Lila loved her wish star, but they also knew it was not practical to bring it on the trip.
"Listen, Lila," dad said. "We understand that you love your wish star, but you can't pack it. It will take up too much space and it might get lost or broken. And you don't need it to make wishes. You can make wishes in your heart, and they will be just as powerful."
"Really?" Lila asked.
"Really," mom said. "Your heart is the most powerful wish maker. And you know what? You can share your wishes with Ben, and he can share his wishes with you. That way, you can both be happy and kind to each other."
Lila thought about it. She looked at her wish star, then at Ben. She smiled.
"Okay," she said. "I will leave my wish star here, and I will make wishes in my heart. And I will share them with Ben. What do you wish, Ben?"
Ben smiled back.
"I wish we have a fun trip, and we see lots of animals, and we eat ice cream," he said.
"Me too," Lila said. "And I wish we are always friends, and we don't fight."
They hugged each other. Mom and dad smiled.
"Good," they said. "Now, let's finish packing and go."
They packed their bags and went on the trip. They had a lot of fun, and they saw lots of animals, and they ate ice cream. And they were always friends, and they didn't fight. And they made wishes in their hearts, and they were powerful.

But Max kept on complaining, no matter what Sam said. Until one day, when Sam asked Max why he kept on complaining. Max said he wanted to find an easier way. But Sam told him nothing comes easy.
So Max worked hard, and eventually his hard work paid off. He discovered a way even more useful than Sam’s way. Sam was so impressed that he asked Max to teach him the new way.
And so the friends learned an important lesson: Hard work is the most useful way to do things. It may not be the easiest, but with hard work, anything can be achieved.

One night, she heard a voice from behind the couch. It was a soft, gentle voice and it said, "You don't have to be scared." The girl was so surprised she jumped from the couch.
"Who said that?" she asked.
The voice answered, "It's me. I live behind the couch and I can see you are scared. I want to tell you something to make you feel better."
The girl was still scared but listened to what the voice had to say. The voice told her stories and made her laugh until she forgot all about feeling scared.
The voice said, "Now, it's time for bed. Sweet dreams!" 
And so, the girl went off to bed feeling safe and secure, grateful for the wonderful friendship she had found behind the couch.

Max’s friend, Abby, saw him trying to climb the log, so she ran to help him. She grabbed one end and said, “Come on, Max, let’s try together! I’ll help you.”
Max and Abby pulled and pushed at the log, struggling hard to get it to move, but it was too heavy for them. Suddenly, a big bear ambled out of the woods and saw what they were doing. It found the log too heavy to move as well, so the bear and Max and Abby worked together and after much hard work, the log finally moved!
Max, Abby and the bear cheered. It had been a lot of work, but it was worth it. They all smiled and hugged each other as they thanked the bear for helping them. Then, the bear waved goodbye and trundled back into the woods. Max and Abby were happy they had been able to overcome the struggle.

Once upon a time, there lived an ordinary mill. It churned day and night, making flour for everyone in the village.
One day, the mill began to creak and groan. It shook like it was about to split in two. The village people rushed to the mill and saw it was about to crumble.
The miller saw it too and sighed.
“What can we do?” he asked.
An old man stepped forward. “The mill has been churning for too long. You need to take a break,” he said.
The miller thought for a moment. “You’re right,” he said. He shut the mill down.
The next day, the mill was alive again. It had been restored and ran smoothly.
Moral: Taking a break is important. If you work too hard without resting, it can lead to a breakdown.

One day, Jack found an axe in the forest. He had never seen an axe before, and he was very surprised. But he was also a bit scared.
Suddenly, he heard a voice call to him from the tree. "Listen," said the voice, "I'll tell you about this axe. It can be used to chop wood and make kindling." Jack listened closely and thought about what the voice had said.
The next day, Jack went back to the forest with some kindling. He was thoughtful, and he knew how to use the axe safely. He made a fire and was able to keep warm as he cooked dinner.
Jack smiled to himself as he felt a sense of satisfaction. He had been very brave and very thoughtful. He was proud of himself.

Once upon a time, there was a kind bear who was walking through the forest. As he was walking, he noticed something strange. It was a bright yellow twist that looked very strange and had a strange texture. Bear wondered what the twist was and decided to have a closer look. 
When he got to the twist, it turned out to be a very dangerous snake. Bear was so scared and the snake hissed at him. Bear quickly stepped back and asked the snake, "What are you doing here?"
The snake replied, "I'm looking for something to twist around. I was searching for a fun activity, but this is too dangerous!"
Bear thought for a moment and said, "Why don't you twist around this big tree? I'm sure you will have a lot of fun and it won't be so dangerous."
The snake thanked Bear and started to twist around the tree. He enjoyed it so much and thanked the kind Bear again. The two said goodbye and Bear continued to walk through the forest.

Tim and Kim were twins who liked to play in the park. They liked to run, jump, slide and swing. But they did not like to share. They always wanted the same toy, the same snack, the same seat. They always fought and cried.
One day, they saw a big statue in the park. It was a statue of a lion and a mouse. The lion had a thorn in his paw and the mouse was helping him. The twins were curious and went closer. They saw a sign that said: "The Lion and the Mouse. A fable by Aesop. The moral is: A kindness is never wasted."
"What is a fable?" asked Tim.
"What is a moral?" asked Kim.
A lady who was sitting on a bench nearby heard them and smiled. She said: "A fable is a story that teaches a lesson. A moral is the lesson that the story teaches. Do you want me to tell you the story of the lion and the mouse?"
The twins nodded and sat down next to the lady. She told them how the lion was the king of the jungle, but he was also very proud and lazy. He did not care about the other animals and he did not listen to anyone. One day, he was sleeping under a tree when a mouse ran over his nose. The lion woke up and was very angry. He caught the mouse and said: "How dare you disturb me? I will eat you for breakfast!"
The mouse was very scared and said: "Please, Mr. Lion, spare me. I did not mean to bother you. I was just looking for food. If you let me go, I will be grateful and I will help you someday."
The lion laughed and said: "You? Help me? How can a tiny mouse help a mighty lion? You are too weak and small. But I am feeling generous today, so I will let you go. But don't ever come near me again."
The mouse thanked the lion and ran away. The lion went back to sleep.
A few days later, the lion was walking in the forest when he stepped on a sharp thorn. The thorn pierced his paw and made him bleed. The lion roared in pain and tried to pull out the thorn, but he could not reach it. He was in trouble and he needed help.
The mouse heard the lion's roar and recognized his voice. He remembered how the lion had spared his life and he decided to help him. He ran to the lion and said: "Mr. Lion, what is wrong? Can I help you?"
The lion was surprised and ashamed to see the mouse. He said: "Oh, it's you. I have a thorn in my paw and it hurts a lot. But you can't help me. You are too weak and small."
The mouse said: "Don't say that, Mr. Lion. You may be big and strong, but I am smart and brave. Let me see your paw. Maybe I can pull out the thorn."
The lion was doubtful, but he was also desperate. He said: "All right, try it. But be careful. Don't hurt me more."
The mouse climbed on the lion's paw and saw the thorn. He used his teeth and his claws and he pulled out the thorn. The lion felt a relief and thanked the mouse. He said: "You are amazing, little mouse. You have saved me. You have proved that you can help me. I was wrong to laugh at you and to be proud and lazy. I am sorry. Can you forgive me?"
The mouse said: "Of course, I forgive you, Mr. Lion. You have also proved that you can be kind and grateful. I am glad that we are friends. The moral is: A kindness is never wasted."
The twins listened to the story and learned the moral. They looked at each other and said: "We are sorry for fighting and crying. We should be kind and share. We should not be proud and lazy. We should be friends."
The lady smiled and said: "That's right, Tim and Kim. You have learned a valuable lesson. Now, go and play and have fun. And remember: A kindness is never wasted."

One day, Lily wanted to try something new. She went to the fridge and found some cheese. She thought cheese would be good with tea and cookies. She put some cheese on the tray and carried it to the table. She said, "Here you are, Mr. Bear. Here you are, Mrs. Bunny. Enjoy your cheese and cookies." She bowed and smiled.
But Mr. Bear and Mrs. Bunny did not like cheese and cookies. They smelled the cheese and made a face. They said, "Yuck! This cheese is disgusting. It is old and moldy. We do not want to eat it. We want to eat fresh and yummy cookies." They pushed the tray away.
Lily was sad and confused. She did not know that cheese could be old and moldy. She thought cheese was always good. She looked at the cheese and saw that it had green spots. She felt sick. She said, "I am sorry, Mr. Bear. I am sorry, Mrs. Bunny. I did not mean to give you disgusting cheese. I thought it was good cheese. I will throw it away and make you new cookies."
She took the tray and went to the trash. She threw away the cheese and washed the tray. She made new cookies and put them on the tray. She carried them to the table. She said, "Here you are, Mr. Bear. Here you are, Mrs. Bunny. Enjoy your new cookies. They are fresh and yummy." She bowed and smiled.
Mr. Bear and Mrs. Bunny were happy and grateful. They smelled the cookies and made a face. They said, "Mmm! These cookies are delicious. They are warm and sweet. We want to eat them. Thank you, Lily. You are a good friend." They pulled the tray closer.
Lily was happy and proud. She had learned something new. She had learned that cheese could be old and moldy. She had learned that old and moldy cheese was disgusting. She had learned that fresh and yummy cookies were delicious. She had learned that her friends liked fresh and yummy cookies. She said, "You are welcome, Mr. Bear. You are welcome, Mrs. Bunny. You are my good friends. Let us have tea and cookies together." She sat down and joined them. They had a nice tea party.

Lily and Ben were twins, but they were very different. Lily liked to play with dolls and draw pictures. Ben liked to play with cars and build blocks. One day, they had to share a tray of cookies that their mom made for them.
"Let's pray first," Lily said. She closed her eyes and folded her hands. "Thank you, God, for the cookies and for mom and dad and for Ben."
Ben rolled his eyes. He did not like to pray. He wanted to eat the cookies right away. He opened his eyes and reached for the tray.
"Hey, stop!" Lily said. She opened her eyes and saw Ben grabbing a cookie. "That's not fair! You have to pray first!"
"No, I don't!" Ben said. He bit the cookie and smiled. "Mmm, yummy!"
Lily felt angry and sad. She wanted to share the cookies with Ben, but he did not care. She started to cry.
Mom heard Lily crying and came to see what was wrong. She saw the tray of cookies and Ben's crumbs on his mouth.
"What happened here?" Mom asked.
"Lily wanted me to pray, but I didn't want to," Ben said.
"Lily, why did you want Ben to pray?" Mom asked.
"Because it's good to thank God for what we have," Lily said.
Mom nodded. She understood how Lily felt. She also understood how Ben felt. She loved them both, even though they were different.
"Ben, I'm glad you like the cookies, but you should respect Lily's choice to pray. Praying is a way of talking to God and showing gratitude. You don't have to pray if you don't want to, but you should wait for Lily to finish before you take a cookie," Mom said.
"Sorry, Lily," Ben said. He felt a little sorry for making Lily cry.
"Lily, I'm proud of you for praying, but you should respect Ben's choice not to pray. Not everyone believes in God or prays the same way. You can pray for yourself and for Ben, but you can't force him to pray with you," Mom said.
"Sorry, Ben," Lily said. She felt a little sorry for being angry at Ben.
Mom smiled. She hugged them both and gave them each another cookie.
"Can we still play together?" Ben asked.
"Of course we can," Lily said.
They ate their cookies and then played with their toys. They were different, but they were still twins. And they still loved each other.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play and learn together. One day, they visit a farm with their class. They see cows, pigs, chickens and sheep. They are happy and curious.
"Look, Tom, this is where cheese comes from!" Lily says, pointing to a big machine that squeezes milk from the cows.
"Wow, cheese is yummy! I want to try some!" Tom says, licking his lips.
They follow the farmer, who shows them how he makes cheese. He cuts, cooks, and shapes the milk into blocks of cheese. He puts some cheese in a basket and gives it to the teacher.
"Thank you, farmer, for the cheese. It is very kind of you," the teacher says.
"You're welcome, teacher. I hope you enjoy it. But be careful, some cheese is very old and strong. It can make your mouth feel funny," the farmer says.
The teacher shares the cheese with the class. They all take a small piece and taste it. Some cheese is soft and mild, some cheese is hard and sharp. Lily and Tom like the cheese. They think it is delicious.
But some children do not like the cheese. They make faces and spit it out. They say the cheese is bad and stinky. They are rude and ungrateful.
"Yuck, this cheese is gross! I don't want it!" one child says, throwing his piece on the ground.
"Me neither! This cheese is nasty! I want candy!" another child says, tossing his piece in the air.
The farmer sees the children being wasteful and disrespectful. He is sad and angry. He scolds the children for their bad manners.
"Shame on you, children, for wasting good cheese. Cheese is a gift from the cows and the land. You should be thankful and polite. If you don't like the cheese, you can say no thank you, but you don't have to throw it away or insult it. That is not smart or nice," the farmer says.
The children feel ashamed and sorry. They apologize to the farmer and the teacher. They promise to be more careful and respectful next time.
Lily and Tom are smart and nice. They thank the farmer again for the cheese. They ask him more questions about the farm and the animals. They learn a lot and have fun.
The moral of the story is: Be thankful and polite for what you have. Don't waste or insult food. Be smart and nice.

A little girl was walking towards him. She asked, "Did you take that copper coin?" 
The old man shivered. He couldn't believe it. He looked down guiltily and said, "Yes, I did take it." 
The little girl glared at him. "That's not fair," she said. "That copper coin doesn't belong to you. You should give it back!" 
The old man felt guilty and shivered again. He knew the little girl was right. He gave back the copper coin and apologized to her. The little girl thanked him and walked away.
The old man watched her go. He learned his lesson that day. It was wrong to take something that belonged to someone else.

Mia was feeling very sad too but she tried to keep a smile on her face. She decided to go play in the park. On her way there she saw a lot of kids playing and she sighed. She wished she could be outside with them but she felt a bit lonely.
Suddenly, she heard somebody calling her. She saw one of her favorite friends holding a present and a birthday cake. Her friends had come to give her a surprise birthday party! 
Mia was so happy! Instead of feeling lonely, she was now surrounded by all the kids playing together. She learned that day that it is important to be kind and caring and that it can make somebody happy even if they don't have a lot of gifts.  Mia was so grateful, and she and her friends ate a healthy birthday cake together.

Once upon a time, there were three friends in the sky. One was a sun, one was a moon, and one was a star. They were always together, shining brightly. The sun and the moon were very jealous of the star, because it twinkled with the most beautiful colours.
One day, the sun said to the star, "I'm the brightest one here - why do they love you so much?"
But the star only smiled and said, "Our light is different, but it is all equally beautiful."
The sun and the moon thought about this and said, "Yes, you're right. Your light is special too."
 
Soon the three friends decided to settle down on earth. The sun shined in the day, the moon glowed in the night, and the star twinkled in the sky. From that day onwards, everyone on earth could enjoy the light of all three friends.
The moral of the story is that it's okay that we are all different. What's important is that we appreciate and enjoy each other's differences.

"Uh oh," she said. "It's gonna rain!"
Her brothers thought it would be fun to keep playing, but Liz couldn't help feeling a little bit scared. She knew heavy rainfall sometimes caused floods and she began to panic. 
Liz begged her brothers to take cover in the barn, but they just laughed and kept playing. Then the rain came down in torrential sheets! Liz knew that the little river near the barn was likely to flood.
She quickly tried to get the boys to a safer place, but it was too late - the barn was already flooding. Her brothers began to scream and cry, while Liz could only stand there in shock. The family had to abandon the ranch and start over again. 
The loss of the ranch was a devastating moment for Liz and her family, but she was also reminded of the power of mother nature. Liz had warned her brothers and tried to get them to safety but they had not listened. Small disasters can quickly lead to much larger endings.

The fairy laughed and said, “My name is Clara. I want to show you something special.” She waved her wand and the fence opened up to reveal a beautiful flower garden. Jimmy’s eyes lit up and he said, “Wow!”
Clara smiled and said, “This is my garden and it is my job to make sure it looks graceful. Now, go explore!”
Jimmy was amazed, so he ran around the garden, looking at all the different kinds of flowers. After he finished exploring, he thanked Clara for showing him such a special place. She smiled and said, “You’re welcome! Now, I must go back to my job of keeping the garden looking graceful. Goodbye!”
And with that, Clara disappeared behind the fence. Jimmy smiled and continued bouncing the ball against the fence, hopeful that one day Clara would come back and reveal her magical garden again.

This pattern happened several more times. Whenever the girl was feeling down, the butterfly would magically appear. She learned that if she was grateful, the butterfly would come and make her happy. She thanked it each time it disappeared into the sky, feeling happier and more grateful each time.

"Ben, what is that?" Anna whispers.
"I don't know. Maybe a monster," Ben says.
They hide under the covers. The noise gets louder. They see the closet door open. They scream.
"Anna! Ben! What's wrong?" Mom comes in. She turns on the light.
"Mom, there is a monster in the closet!" Anna cries.
Mom looks in the closet. She smiles.
"No, there is no monster. It is just your clothes. They fell off the hanger. See?" Mom shows them the clothes.
Anna and Ben feel silly. They laugh.
"Sorry, Mom. We were scared," Ben says.
"It's okay. It's normal to be scared sometimes. But there is nothing to be afraid of. Your clothes are not monsters. They are just clothes," Mom says.
She hugs them and tucks them in.
"Good night, Anna. Good night, Ben. I love you," Mom says.
"Good night, Mom. We love you too," Anna and Ben say.
They close their eyes and fall asleep. They are not scared anymore.

Tom was a boy who liked to polish things. He had a cloth and a bottle of polish that he used to make his toys and shoes shiny. He was very proud of his work and liked to show it to his friends.
One day, he went to the park with his mom and saw a big statue of a king. The king had a crown and a sword and a long coat. Tom thought the statue looked dull and dirty. He wanted to make it shiny like his toys and shoes.
He ran to the statue and climbed on it. He took out his cloth and polish and started to rub the king's face. He did not see the sign that said "Do not touch". He did not hear his mom calling him to come down. He did not notice the people staring at him.
"Hey, what are you doing?" a loud voice said. Tom looked up and saw a man in a uniform. He had a badge and a hat and a whistle. He was a guard. He was angry.
"I'm polishing the king," Tom said. "He looks sad and dirty. I want to make him happy and shiny."
The guard frowned and blew his whistle. He grabbed Tom and lifted him off the statue. He scolded him and told him he was not allowed to touch the statue. He said he could damage it and get in trouble.
Tom felt scared and embarrassed. He did not mean to do anything bad. He just wanted to polish the king. He started to cry and said he was sorry.
The guard softened and gave Tom a tissue. He said he understood that Tom liked to polish things, but he had to be careful and respectful of the statue. He said the statue was very old and important and needed to be protected. He said Tom could polish other things, like his bike or his spoon, but not the statue.
Tom nodded and wiped his tears. He said he was sorry again and promised not to touch the statue anymore. He hugged his mom and said he wanted to go home.
The guard smiled and said it was okay. He said he hoped Tom learned his lesson and would be more careful next time. He said he liked to polish things too, when he was a boy. He said he had a polish for his badge and his hat and his whistle. He said he would show Tom how to use it, if he wanted.
Tom smiled and said yes. He said he liked the guard and his polish. He said he wanted to be a guard when he grew up. He said he would polish his badge and his hat and his whistle every day.
The guard laughed and said he was glad. He said he would be happy to have Tom as a friend and a helper. He said he would teach Tom how to be a good guard and how to respect the king. He said he would let Tom polish his badge and his hat and his whistle, once in a while.
Tom was happy. He said he liked the king and his statue. He said he wanted to make him happy and shiny, but not with his polish. He said he would make him happy and shiny with his smile and his wave and his thank you. He said he would be a good boy and a good guard and a good friend. He said he learned his lesson and would not be embarrassed again.

The twins go back to their patch and make a pile of radishes, carrots and lettuce. They leave a note that says, "For the rabbit. From Sam and Mia. We want to be your friends."

She tried to reach the jar, but it was too high for her. She looked around and saw a chair. She had an idea. She pushed the chair to the table and climbed on it. She was very careful not to fall. She stretched her arm and tried to lift the jar of honey.
But the jar was too heavy for her. She could not lift it. She pulled and pulled, but the jar did not move. She felt sad and frustrated. She started to cry.
Then, she heard a voice. It was her mom. She came to the garden and saw Lily on the chair. She asked her what was wrong. Lily pointed to the jar of honey and said, "I want honey, but I can't lift it. It's too heavy."
Her mom smiled and hugged her. She said, "Don't cry, Lily. I can help you. Honey is very heavy, but it is also very sticky. If you lift it, it might spill and make a mess. How about we share some honey on a slice of bread? That way, you can taste the honey and not waste it."
Lily nodded and smiled. She liked that idea. She got down from the chair and followed her mom to the kitchen. They made some honey bread and ate it together. It was delicious. Lily thanked her mom and gave her a kiss. She was happy. She learned that honey is heavy and sticky, but also sweet and yummy. And she learned that mom is always there to help her.

Lily and Ben love to play at the beach. They like to make castles with sand and shells. They also like to decorate their castles with flowers and stones.
One day, they find a big pink bucket near the water. They are very happy. They think it is a gift for them. They fill the bucket with sand and turn it over. They make a big pink tower.
They want to decorate the tower with shells and flowers. They look around and see many pretty things. They see a starfish, a feather, a leaf and a coin. They run to get them and put them on the tower.
But when they come back, they see a big wave. The wave is coming to the tower. They are scared. They shout, "No, no, no! Stop, wave, stop!"
But the wave does not stop. It hits the tower and washes it away. The sand, the shells, the flowers, the starfish, the feather, the leaf and the coin are gone. The bucket is gone too.
Lily and Ben are sad. They cry. They want their tower back. They want their bucket back.
But then they see something shiny in the water. It is the coin. The wave brought it back to them. They smile. They think it is a gift for them. They run to get it and put it in their pocket.
They say, "Thank you, wave, thank you!"
They hug each other. They are happy again. They decide to make a new castle with sand and shells. They also decide to decorate it with the coin. They think it will make it very special.

Ben kneels down to see the pizza. He does not like olives. He thinks they are yucky. He makes a face.
"No, thank you, Sara. I do not like olives. They are yucky. Can I have something else?" Ben says.
Sara is sad. She worked hard on her pizza. She thinks it is yummy. She does not want to waste it.
"Please, Ben, try a bite. Maybe you will like it. Olives are good for you. They are healthy." Sara says.
Ben does not want to hurt Sara's feelings. He is a good friend. He decides to try a bite. He picks up a small piece of the pizza and puts it in his mouth. He chews slowly. He is surprised. The pizza is not yucky. It is yummy. He likes olives.
"Mmm, Sara, this is yummy. You are a good chef. I like olives. Can I have some more?" Ben says.
Sara is happy. She smiles. She is glad Ben likes her pizza. She shares it with him. They eat the pizza together. They are good friends. They have fun.

Tim and Sam are friends. They like to play at the gym. The gym has many toys and games. They can run, jump, swing, and slide. They have fun at the gym.
One day, Tim and Sam see a new boy at the gym. His name is Ben. Ben has no toys and no games. He has only a ball. He kicks the ball by himself. He looks sad.
Tim and Sam want to play with Ben. They go to him and say, "Hi, Ben. Do you want to play with us? We have many toys and games. You can share with us."
Ben looks at Tim and Sam. He says, "No, thank you. I have my own toys and games. They are at home. They are better than yours. I don't need to share."
Tim and Sam are surprised. They think Ben is lying. They say, "Really? What toys and games do you have at home? Can you tell us?"
Ben thinks for a moment. He says, "I have a big car, a big train, a big robot, a big dinosaur, and a big castle. They are all mine. They are all shiny and new. They are all fun."
Tim and Sam are more surprised. They think Ben is lying more. They say, "Wow, that sounds amazing. Can we see them? Can we come to your home?"
Ben shakes his head. He says, "No, you can't. My home is far away. You can't find it. You can't come. You can't see. You can only play with your toys and games. I can only play with my ball."
Tim and Sam are sad. They think Ben is poor. They think he has no toys and games at home. They think he is lying to hide his sadness. They want to help him. They want to be his friends.
They say, "Ben, we are sorry. We don't believe you. We think you are lying. We think you are poor. We think you have no toys and games at home. We think you are sad. We want to help you. We want to be your friends. Please, don't lie to us. Please, play with us. Please, share with us. We have enough for all. We can have fun together."
Ben looks at Tim and Sam. He sees their kind eyes and their smiling faces. He feels their warm hearts and their gentle words. He feels ashamed of his lies. He feels sorry for his pride. He feels lonely for his ball. He feels happy for their offer. He says, "Tim, Sam, thank you. You are right. I am lying. I am poor. I have no toys and games at home. I am sad. I need your help. I need your friendship. Please, let me play with you. Please, let me share with you. I have only a ball, but I can give it to you. We can have fun together."
Tim and Sam are glad. They hug Ben. They say, "Ben, welcome. You are our friend. You don't need to lie to us. You don't need to be poor. You don't need to be sad. You have us. We have you. We have many toys and games. We have a ball. We have fun together."
They take Ben to the gym. They show him their toys and games. They play with his ball. They run, jump, swing, and slide. They have fun at the gym. They are friends.

Lila and Ben were playing in the backyard. They had a big box and some shiny paper. They wanted to make a pretend spaceship.
"Let's deliver some crystals to the moon," Lila said. She had a necklace with a blue crystal that sparkled in the sun.
"OK, but we have to be careful. There are fierce aliens on the moon," Ben said. He had a toy laser gun that made funny noises.
They climbed into the box and pretended to fly. They made whoosh and beep sounds. They saw the moon in the sky. It was round and white.
"Look, there's a landing spot," Lila said. She pointed to a patch of dirt. "Let's go and give the crystal to the moon people."
They got out of the box and walked slowly. They held hands. They saw something move behind a bush. It was green and hairy. It had big eyes and sharp teeth. It was an alien!
"Roar!" The alien jumped out and ran towards them. It wanted the crystal.
"Help!" Lila and Ben screamed. They dropped the crystal and ran back to the box. They closed the flap and locked it.
"Go away, you fierce alien!" Ben shouted. He waved his laser gun. "We don't want to play with you!"
The alien picked up the crystal and looked at it. It liked the shiny thing. It smiled and made a friendly noise. It wanted to play with Lila and Ben.
"Hello, I'm Zog. I'm not fierce. I'm lonely. Can I be your friend?" The alien said. It knocked on the box.
Lila and Ben heard the alien. They were scared, but also curious. They opened the flap and peeked out. They saw the alien holding the crystal. It looked sad.
"Hi, I'm Lila. This is Ben. We're sorry we ran away. We thought you were fierce," Lila said.
"I'm sorry I scared you. I just wanted to see the crystal. It's so pretty. Can I share it with you?" Zog said.
Lila and Ben nodded. They came out of the box and smiled. They gave Zog a hug. They played with the crystal and the laser gun. They had fun.
They became friends. They delivered the crystal to the moon people. They flew back to Earth. They had a great adventure.

"I'm digging a home," said the mole.
"Oh, can I help?" asked Lily.
"Yes, please," said the mole.
Lily got a shovel and helped the mole dig its home. When they were finished, the mole was very happy. "Thank you for helping me," said the mole.
"You're welcome," said Lily. "I had fun getting dirty with you."
From that day on, Lily visited the mole every day and they became the best of friends.

She bent down to take a closer look and suddenly, the jug toppled over and all the water spilled out. It created a small pond around the flower.
Sarah felt badly and she tried her best to mop up all the water, but it was too much. Her mom came over to help her and together they gathered a few empty jugs from the shed and started filling them with the water. Within an hour, the water was all gone and the flower looked very modest, standing in the damp grass.
The next day, Sarah and her mom took the empty jugs to the lake. They filled the jugs with lake water and soon, the jug and the flower both had water. The flower was very happy and Sarah was happy that the flower was doing better.
But little did they know, the lake water was not that clean. The water in the jug started to rot and an awful smell filled the air. Sarah and her mom had to throw the jug away. Thankfully, the flower was now in better shape and Sarah learned an important lesson.

The water kept getting higher and higher until her feet were nearly in it. She didn't dare move, but she was a little scared. The flood was so powerful that it was beginning to wash away the sand beneath her feet.
But the little girl wouldn't move. She kept insisting that she would stand her ground and not be scared. Suddenly, the waves stopped and the water began to go down. The girl had won - she had stayed and faced the flood. She had been brave and competitive enough to beat the water. She was brave and big and strong, and she was beaming with pride.

Lucy and Tom ran back to their houses just as the rain started to fall. Inside, they watched as the wind blew and the rain poured. The hurricane was very big and loud. After a while, the storm stopped, and the sky became clear again.
Lucy went outside to see if the kite was still there. She found it stuck in a tree. Tom came out too, and they both worked together to get the kite down. They were happy they had listened to the warning about the hurricane and stayed safe inside. Now they could play with the kite again on another clear day.

Tim and his mom sat down with the toy phone. They took turns telling jokes to each other. Tim's mom said, "Why did the chicken cross the road?" Tim thought and said, "I don't know, Mom. Why?" His mom said, "To get to the other side!" They both laughed.
Tim told a joke too. He said, "Why do cows wear bells?" His mom said, "I don't know, Tim. Why?" Tim said, "Because their horns don't work!" They both laughed again.
They kept telling jokes and laughing. Tim felt happy again. The bad day was gone. From that day on, Tim and his mom would tell jokes to each other when they felt bad. And the toy phone was always there to help them share their jokes.

One day, when the sun was out and bright, Macy's mom and dad decided to take her for a walk. They grabbed their hats and went to the beach. Macy was very excited and danced around in the sand.
Macy's dad said, "Let's build a sandcastle." Macy asked, "Will you help me, Dad?" Her dad smiled and said "Yes, of course!"
They scooped and molded the sand until they made a big sandcastle. Macy's mom said, "That's silly, Macy!" Macy giggled and said, "It's fun!"
Macy's mom and dad encouraged her to keep building  the sandcastle. "We can make it higher and higher," they said. They stayed together and kept building until they made the biggest, silliest sandcastle that Macy had ever seen.
Macy looked up at the bright sun and felt happy. She said, "This is great! I love sandcastles". Her mom and dad smiled as they watched Macy run around the sandcastle. They were proud of her.

 Once upon a time, there was a clever fox. He was exploring the forest when he saw smoke in the distance. He knew it was a fire and he had to put it out. So he raced to the spot, but there wasn't enough water to put it out.
The fox looked around, and spotted a lake. He ran towards it, and started to dip his paws in the lake, then throwing the water at the fire to put it out. But no matter how hard he tried, the fire wouldn't stop.
Just then, he heard a voice. It was a farmer, standing nearby. The farmer said, "Hey Fox, what are you doing?" The fox replied, "I'm trying to stop this fire." The farmer said, "That's no good! You need to put something in the fire to make it go away!"
The fox thought for a moment, then he had a clever idea. He picked up some leaves and twigs and threw them in the fire. The leaves and twigs smothered the flames and soon, the fire was completely out. 
The fox was very happy. He had saved the forest!

"Good day, sheep," said the hairdresser. "What would you like today?"
The sheep was a bit nervous and replied: "I would like you to remove some of my wool."
The hairdresser nodded happily, saying: “No problem! I will remove some of your wool and then do something else special.”
The hairdresser started to remove the sheep's wool, while the sheep watched nervously. The hairdresser began to comb the sheep's wool, blow it to make it look fluffy, and even trim the edges so that it looked neat.
Once it was finished, the hairdresser said: “There you go! How does it look?”
The sheep was very happy and said: “It looks great! Thank you very much!”
The hairdresser beamed and said: “You’re welcome! Have a great day!”
The sheep thanked the hairdresser again, then left with her brand new look. She was so happy, she felt like she was a new sheep!

One day the princess went outside to use her magic arrow. She looked around for something to shoot. Suddenly, she noticed a little bird sitting on a tree. 
The princess thought it would be fun to make the bird move with her arrow. She took aim, held her breath and shot her arrow. As soon as the arrow hit the tree, the bird flew away. 
The princess was delighted. She said to herself," That was so much fun!" 
Then she saw a group of other birds sitting in the field. She took aim and shot another arrow at the group of birds. Suddenly, all the birds flew away, but one. The bird refused to move. 
The princess was surprised and asked," Why don't you fly away like the others? Are you not scared?". 
The bird replied,"No, I'm not scared. You have been very generous to us today." 
The princess was touched by the bird's kind words. She smiled and said," You are very brave. You can stay here as long as you want." 
The bird thanked her and sat in the field with the other birds. The princess smiled and returned home with her magic arrow.

Billy wanted to go the other way, but Sally insisted. When they got closer, Sally was delighted when she saw it was a delicate woodland flower! But then, Billy heard something different. He heard a demand coming from behind them. They both turned around to see a man with a big weapon pointed at them. 
The man demanded they give him the flower. Sally started to cry, but Billy stepped in front of her to protect her. He told the man there was no way he was getting the flower.
The man got angry and said he would hurt them if they didn't give it to him. Sally and Billy thought quickly and made a plan to get away. Sally very quietly grabbed the flower and hid it in her pocket, and Billy yelled for help.
The man got scared and ran away. Sally and Billy hugged each other, happy to have outsmarted the man. They had saved the delicate flower and become heroes!

Once upon a time, there was a deaf bush. The bush couldn't hear anything. Every morning, birds would sing and other animals would talk, but the bush couldn't hear any of it.
One day, a little bunny named Sarah stumbled across the deaf bush. "Oh no," she said. "This bush can't hear anything!"
Sarah knew that she had to do something to help restore the bush. She grabbed a nearby watering can, filled it with water and then watered the bush.
Next, Sarah plucked some petals from nearby flowers and carefully placed them around the bush. Finally, she found some big rocks nearby and used them to make a circle around the bush.
"Now," she said. "Let's see if this helps."
To her surprise, when Sarah finished, the bush was no longer deaf! The birds began to sing, the animals began to talk and the bush even joined in by swaying in the wind.
Sarah smiled in delight. She had just learned how to restore a deaf bush!

But when Benny opened the cooler, he saw that it was full of carrots! Benny felt guilty for taking the carrots, but he was so hungry that he couldn't resist. Just as he was about to take a bite, he heard a loud growl. It was the owner of the cooler, a big bear named Barry. 
Benny knew he had made a mistake and felt even more guilty. He quickly hopped away, but Barry chased after him. Benny was scared, but he knew he had to make things right. So he hopped back to the cooler and put all the carrots back inside. Barry saw this and was impressed by Benny's honesty. From that day on, Barry and Benny became good friends and Benny never felt guilty again.

Days went by and Jack had to come back to the ranch without Brownie. He was very lonely and sad. He sat on his porch and cried. Suddenly, he heard a neighing sound. He got up and ran towards the sound. It was Brownie! He had come back! Jack was so happy and hugged his horse tightly. But then, he noticed that Brownie was hurt. He had a broken leg and couldn't walk anymore. Jack knew he had to put his friend down. He was heartbroken and cried all night long.

Once upon a time, there was a prince who lived in a big castle. He was very selfish and didn't like to share his toys with anyone. One day, he went to the park to play with his ball.
At the park, he saw a little boy crying because he lost his toy. The prince didn't want to help him and said, "I don't care about your toy. I only care about mine." The little boy was sad and walked away.
Later that day, the prince went back to the castle and played with his ball. Suddenly, he saw a mark on his ball. He realized that he had been playing too rough and the ball was now broken. He felt sad and wished he had been nicer to the little boy at the park.
The next day, the prince went back to the park and saw the same little boy. He went up to him and said, "I'm sorry for being selfish yesterday. I want to share my toys with you." The little boy smiled and they became friends. From that day on, the prince learned that it's important to be kind to others and not just think about himself.

One day, Blue saw Brown and asked, "Hey Brown! Do you want to come fly with me?" Brown replied, "No thank you, Blue. I like to stay organized and hop in the snow." 
Blue flew away and enjoyed soaring in the sky. But suddenly, a big storm came and Blue got lost. Blue tried to find the way back but couldn't. Brown noticed that Blue was missing and went to search for Blue. Brown found Blue lying on the ground, hurt and unable to fly. Brown cried and said, "Oh no, Blue! I wish you had stayed with me in the snow. Now you can't fly anymore." 
From that day on, Blue had to stay on the ground and never soar in the sky again. Brown felt sad and regretted not going with Blue. They both learned that sometimes it's better to stay safe and be together with friends.

Once upon a time there was a bald man named Bob. Bob was walking in the park one day when he saw a funny looking poke in a tree. Curious, Bob poked it with his finger. Suddenly, out from the poke came a cork and a bottle of red wine! Bob was so excited that he couldn't help but take a big sip of the wine.
Just then, a voice called out from behind Bob. "Hey, what do you think you're doing?" It was Bob's old friend Tom! Tom was a balding man who had been walking in the park with his daughter.
Bob, who was a bit embarrassed, said to Tom, "I thought I saw a funny poke in the tree, so I poked it and it gave me a bottle of wine!"
Tom replied, "Now, now, Bob! Drinking wine in the park isn't allowed. You should put it back!" Bob listened to Tom and returned the bottle of wine to the poke. He thanked his friend for his kindness and promised never to do it again.
The end.

The puppy started to walk around the stand, exploring his new, tiny size. But soon, he got scared. He tried to run away, but his tiny legs could not carry him very far.
The puppy was stuck. He was too small now to jump over the high walls around him. He was desperate to escape, but he could not.
Suddenly, the puppy heard someone calling to him; it was an old man. The man had seen the puppy shrinking and was amazed. He said it was a magic newspaper - and it had granted the puppy's wish to be small.
The old man helped the puppy to escape. Together, they found the forgotten magic newspaper that had given the puppy such an enormous wish.

Once upon a time there was an otter who lived in the river. He was always happy and friendly to everyone he saw.
One day, he noticed an angry bird standing on a log near the water. The otter swam over to him and said, "Hello, are you okay?"
The bird was too angry to speak so he just stared at the otter.
The otter thought for a moment, then offered: "If it would help, I could listen to your story".
The bird thought about it and then agreed, so the otter closed his eyes and listened. As the bird spoke, the otter's heart grew closer to the bird, until the bird's anger turned to  tears.
The otter opened his eyes and said softly, "Your story is over now, and you no longer have to be alone".
The bird thanked the otter, and they said goodbye, each one smiling and grateful.
The moral of the story is that sometimes it takes courage to deal with our anger. We don't have to handle it all by ourselves, as a listening ear can transform our hearts and bring us closer together.

"Wow, look at the truck!" Ben says. "It is so big and red!"
"I want to see the hose!" Mia says. "Maybe it can spray water!"
They run to the truck. A fireman is sitting in the front. He smiles at them.
"Hello, kids. Do you like the truck?" he asks.
"Yes, we do!" Ben and Mia say.
"Do you want to see the hose?" the fireman asks.
"Yes, please!" Ben and Mia say.
The fireman gets out of the truck. He takes them to the back. He shows them the hose. It is coiled up on a reel.
"This is the hose. We use it to spray water on fires. It helps to cool down the heat and stop the flames," he explains.
"Can we touch it?" Ben asks.
"Sure, but be careful. It is very heavy and strong," the fireman says.
Ben and Mia touch the hose. It feels hard and smooth. They try to lift it, but it is too heavy.
"Wow, this is heavy!" Mia says.
"It is. We need a lot of water to fight fires," the fireman says.
"Can we hear the horn?" Ben asks.
"Sure, but cover your ears. It is very loud," the fireman says.

Timmy was so happy that the frog saved him. "Thank you, Mr. Frog!" he said. The frog just smiled and waved goodbye as he hopped away. From that day on, Timmy always looked for the green frog in the park, hoping to see him again.

Sara and Ben were playing in the attic. They liked to look at the old things that their grandma kept there. They found an ancient book with strange pictures and words. Sara opened the book and read a page out loud.
"Shrink, shrink, shrink, until you are as small as a pin. Then you can see the wonders of the world that are hidden from your eyes."
Suddenly, Sara and Ben felt a strange tingling in their bodies. They looked at each other and screamed. They were shrinking! They became smaller and smaller, until they were as tiny as ants. They saw the dust and cobwebs on the floor, the cracks and holes in the walls, and the spiders and mice that lived in the attic. They were scared and wanted to go back to their normal size.
"Help, help!" they cried. "How do we get big again?"
They looked at the book, but it was too far away and too big for them to read. They tried to climb on a chair, but it was too high and too slippery. They saw the ceiling above them, but it was too far and too dark. They felt hopeless and alone.
Then they heard a voice. It was their grandma. She had heard their screams and came to the attic. She saw the book and the tiny children on the floor. She picked up the book and read the next page.
"Grow, grow, grow, until you are as big as you were. Then you will appreciate the beauty of the world that you have in your eyes."
She said the words out loud and sprinkled some water on Sara and Ben. They felt a warm glow in their bodies. They started to grow! They became bigger and bigger, until they were back to their normal size. They hugged their grandma and thanked her for saving them.
"I'm sorry, grandma," Sara said. "We were curious and we read the book. We didn't know it was magic."
"It's okay, my dears," grandma said. "But you should be careful with things that you don't understand. Sometimes they can be dangerous or harmful. And you should be grateful for what you have. The world is full of wonders, but you don't need to shrink or grow to see them. You just need to open your eyes and your heart."
Sara and Ben nodded and smiled. They learned their lesson and never played with the ancient book again. They enjoyed the attic and the old things, but they also loved the outside and the new things. They saw the wonders of the world in every size and shape.

"Would you like to have some of these?" Captain Jack asked. "You can choose one thing each. I have plenty to share. I am a generous man." Lila and Sam thanked him and looked at the chest. They had a hard time deciding what to pick. They liked everything.

Lila and Sam ran to their mom and dad and showed them their gifts. They told them about Captain Jack and his treasure. Their mom and dad smiled and hugged them. They said they were very lucky and very kind. They enjoyed their day at the shore.

"Ow, Tim, that hurt!" Sam said. "The stick hit my leg!"
"I'm sorry, Sam, I didn't mean to hurt you," Tim said. "Let's try again with another stick."
"No, Tim, I don't want to try again. It's too hard and dangerous. And maybe the apples are not good. Maybe they belong to someone else. Maybe they are unknown apples," Sam said.
"Unknown apples? What does that mean?" Tim asked.
"It means we don't know where they come from, or who they are for, or what they taste like. Maybe they are sour, or bitter, or rotten. Maybe they have worms, or bugs, or poison. Maybe they are not for us," Sam said.
"Wow, Sam, you are very smart. You know a lot of words. How do you know all that?" Tim asked.
"I know because I listen to Mom and Dad. They always tell us to be careful and respectful and not to take things that are not ours. They repeat it a lot, so I remember it," Sam said.
"Oh, I see. I should listen to Mom and Dad too. They repeat it because they love us and want us to be safe and happy. I'm sorry I didn't listen before. Let's go home and tell them we love them too," Tim said.
"OK, Tim, let's go home. And maybe they will give us some good apples that they bought from the store," Sam said.
Tim and Sam hugged and walked home. They learned that it is better to listen to their parents and not to take unknown things. They also learned that apples are not always easy to get, but they are always sweet to share.

Then the man showed Jack how to look through a clear telescope. It was amazing! Jack could see the clouds and the birds high in the sky. It was so beautiful that he laughed out loud again.
The man chuckled and said, "You must really like looking through this telescope!" Jack nodded his head and said, "Yes, I do!"
The man told Jack that if he kept laughing and looking up at the sky, he would have a great life. Jack smiled and thanked the man for the clear telescope. He walked away with a big smile on his face knowing that he had learned an important lesson.

Just then, his friend Benny the bird flew by. "What's wrong, Sammy?" Benny asked.
"This acorn is broken," Sammy said sadly. "I can't eat it."
Benny looked at the broken acorn and said, "Don't worry, Sammy. I'll help you find a good acorn to eat." 
So, Benny and Sammy searched together and found a big, beautiful acorn that was not broken. Sammy was very happy and thanked Benny for helping him. They both played together in the trees, happy and content. The end.

One day, they decided to paint outside. It was a sunny and warm day. They took their paints and papers and went to the backyard. They saw a big pool of water. It looked like a swim. They wanted to swim and paint at the same time.
"Let's paint in the water!" Tim said.
"OK, that sounds fun!" Mia said.
They put their papers on the ground and dipped their brushes in the water. They made swirls and splashes and dots on the papers. They laughed and giggled. They did not see that the water was filthy. It had mud and dirt and bugs and leaves. Their papers became brown and dirty. Their clothes became wet and stained. Their faces and hands became filthy too.
They painted for a long time. They did not hear their mom calling them. She came to the backyard and saw them. She was shocked and angry.
"What are you doing?" she yelled. "You are filthy! You ruined your papers and clothes and the water! You have to clean up right now!"
Tim and Mia looked at their mom. They looked at each other. They looked at their paintings. They did not understand why she was mad. They thought they had made beautiful art. They were sad and confused. They did not want to clean up. They wanted to swim and paint more.

One day, Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big box under a tree. It was brown and had a red ribbon on it.
"Look, a present!" Lily said. "Maybe it is for us!"
Ben was curious. He wanted to see what was inside. He ran to the box and pulled the ribbon. Then he tried to tear the paper.
"Stop, Ben!" Lily shouted. "That is not nice! Maybe it is for someone else!"
But Ben did not listen. He tore the paper more and more. He made a big hole in the box. Then he saw something shiny and bright.
"Wow, what is that?" Ben said. He reached his hand inside the box.
Suddenly, a loud noise came from the box. It was like a firework. Ben jumped back and screamed. Lily ran to him and hugged him.
"Are you okay, Ben?" Lily asked. She was scared.
Ben nodded. He was okay, but he was also sorry. He looked at the box. It was full of sparks. They were red and yellow and blue. They made the box glow and crackle.
"What are they?" Ben asked. He had never seen sparks before.
"I don't know," Lily said. "They are mysterious. Maybe they are magic."
They watched the sparks for a while. They were pretty, but they were also dangerous. They did not touch the box again.
Then they heard a voice. It was a man. He was wearing a hat and a coat. He had a big smile on his face.
"Hello, children," he said. "Did you like my surprise?"
He walked to the box and picked it up. He did not seem to mind the sparks.
"Who are you?" Lily asked. She did not trust the man.
"I am a magician," he said. "I was going to do a show in the park. But I forgot my box here. I am glad you found it. It is a special box. It makes sparks when you open it. It is fun, but it is also a trick. You have to be careful with it."
He winked at them and laughed.
"Sorry, mister," Ben said. He felt bad for tearing the paper.
"That's okay, Ben," the man said. He was kind. "You were just curious. Curiosity is good. It helps you learn new things. But you also have to be respectful. Sometimes things are not what they seem. Sometimes they are mysterious. And sometimes they are not for you."
He gave them each a candy and a balloon. Then he waved goodbye and left with his box.
Lily and Ben looked at each other. They had learned a lesson. They had also had an adventure. They smiled and held their balloons. They went back to playing in the park. They did not tear any more paper.

Tim and Mia liked to play in the pool. They had a big shark toy that they could ride on. Tim wanted to show Mia how brave he was. He said, "Watch me raise the shark over my head!"
Tim grabbed the shark and tried to lift it up. But the shark was too heavy and slippery. Tim lost his balance and fell into the water. The shark landed on his head and made a loud splash.
Mia laughed and said, "That was funny, Tim! You look like a shark hat!" Tim felt embarrassed. He did not like to be laughed at. He wanted to be brave and strong.
Tim got out of the water and took the shark off his head. He said, "It's not funny, Mia! It's hard to raise a shark. You try it!"
Mia said, "OK, I will try it. But I will be careful." She took the shark and lifted it up slowly. She raised it over her head and smiled. She said, "Look, Tim! I did it! I raised the shark!"
Tim felt more embarrassed. He did not like to be shown up by Mia. He said, "That's easy, Mia! You just got lucky. Let me try again!"
Tim and Mia took turns trying to raise the shark. Sometimes they did it, and sometimes they did not. They had fun and forgot to be embarrassed. They liked to play with the shark.

One day, Tom and Anna went to the zoo with their mom. They saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and elephants. They liked to watch them and learn their names.
When they came to the rhino, Tom was very curious. He pointed at the big thing on its nose and asked, "Mom, what is that?"
Mom smiled and said, "That is a horn, Tom. It is part of the rhino's body. It helps the rhino to protect itself and to find food."
Tom nodded and said, "I see. It is a big horn. Can I touch it?"
Mom shook her head and said, "No, Tom. You cannot touch it. It is not safe. The rhino might get angry and hurt you. You have to stay behind the fence and look from far away."
Tom was a little sad, but he understood. He said, "OK, Mom. I will not touch it. But can I ask it a question?"
Mom laughed and said, "Sure, Tom. You can ask it a question. But I don't think it will answer you. It does not speak our language."
Tom did not care. He went closer to the fence and shouted, "Hello, rhino! Why do you have a horn? Is it fun? Do you like it?"
The rhino did not say anything. It just looked at Tom with its small eyes and snorted. Then it turned around and walked away.
Anna, who was watching, giggled and said, "Tom, you are crazy. The rhino does not care about your question. It is busy eating grass. Come on, let's go see the giraffes. They have long necks and spots. Maybe they will talk to you."

"Yes, it is. But I have an idea. Let's make the loop more fun!" Sara says.
She takes some books and puts them under one part of the loop. She raises the track with the books. Now the loop has a hill.
"Wow, Sara, that is cool! But is it not difficult for the train to go up the hill?" Ben asks.
"Let's see!" Sara says. She pushes the train with her hand. The train goes up the hill, but then it stops. It cannot go down the other side. It falls off the track.
"Oh no, Sara, the train is broken!" Ben says.
"It is okay, Ben. We can fix it. And we can make the hill smaller. Then the train can go over the loop and not fall off." Sara says.
They take some books away and make the hill smaller. They put the train back on the track. They watch it go over the loop and smile.
"Yay, Sara, you did it! The loop is fun and not difficult!" Ben says.
"Thank you, Ben. You are a good friend. I like to play with you and the trains." Sara says.
