Tim and Lily were playing in the garden with their grandma. They liked to help her water the flowers and smell the herbs. Grandma had many herbs in pots and baskets. She said they were good for cooking and making tea.
One day, they saw a big bird on the fence. It was black and shiny, with a long beak and a loud voice. It looked at the herbs and made a noise. "Caw, caw, caw!" it said. Tim and Lily were curious. They wanted to see the bird closer.
They ran to the fence and waved their hands. "Hello, bird!" they said. "What are you doing here?" The bird looked at them and tilted its head. "Caw, caw, caw!" it said again. Then it flew to the nearest basket of herbs and grabbed some with its beak. It scattered the herbs all over the ground.
"Hey, stop that!" Tim shouted. "Those are grandma's herbs!" Lily cried. They tried to chase the bird away, but it was too fast and clever. It flew from basket to basket, scattering more herbs. Tim and Lily were angry and sad. They loved grandma's herbs.
Grandma heard the noise and came out of the house. She saw the bird and the mess. She was not angry or sad. She smiled and said, "Don't worry, my dears. That's a crow. He likes to eat herbs. He thinks they are tasty and healthy. He's an elderly bird, you know. He's been coming here for years. He's my friend."
Tim and Lily were surprised. They looked at the crow and the herbs. They did not understand. How could grandma be friends with a bird that scattered her herbs? Grandma saw their faces and said, "It's okay. I have plenty of herbs. I don't mind sharing some with the crow. He's a smart and funny bird. He likes to talk to me. Sometimes he brings me shiny things. He's a good bird."
Tim and Lily thought about it. They decided to be nice to the crow. They said, "Hello, crow. We're sorry we yelled at you. You can have some herbs. But please don't scatter them too much. Grandma likes them neat and tidy."
The crow looked at them and nodded. He said, "Caw, caw, caw!" He took some herbs and flew away. He left a shiny coin on the fence. Grandma picked it up and said, "Thank you, crow. You're very generous. Come back anytime."
Tim and Lily smiled. They hugged grandma and said, "We love you, grandma. And we love your herbs. And we love the crow, too. He's a good bird." Grandma hugged them back and said, "I love you, too, my dears. And I love the crow, too. He's a good friend." They all laughed and went inside to make some tea with the herbs.

"Wow, Lila, you did it!" Ben says.
He picks up the green ball. He smells it. It smells sour. He makes a face.
"Yuck, Lila, this is not a ball. This is a lime!" Ben says.
He gives the lime to Lila. Lila smells it too. She makes a face.
"Yuck, Ben, you are right. This is a lime!" Lila says.
They hear a noise. They turn around. They see a big cat. The cat is orange and black. It has stripes. It has sharp teeth. It has a long tail. It is a tiger. It is wild.
"Look, Lila, a cat!" Ben says.
"No, Ben, not a cat. A tiger!" Lila says.
They are scared. They drop the lime. They run to the house. They scream for mom.

"Yes, mom, we want to play with it!" Lila and Ben say.

One day, they see a big dog. The dog is brown and furry. It has a long tail and a wet nose. The dog runs to them and barks. Lily and Max are scared. They pause and hold hands.
"Go away, dog!" Lily says. "We don't want to play with you!"
But the dog does not go away. It jumps and tries to get the ball and the kite. It makes a mess. Lily and Max are sad. They want their toys back.
"Help, help!" Max says. "Who can help us?"
Then they see a man. The man is tall and kind. He has a hat and a whistle. He is a park ranger. He hears Max and Lily. He comes to them and sees the dog.
"Hey, boy!" the park ranger says. "What are you doing here? You are not supposed to be in the park without a leash!"
He blows his whistle and the dog stops. The dog looks at the park ranger and wags his tail. The park ranger smiles and pets the dog.
"Don't worry, kids," he says. "This dog is not bad. He is just playful. He belongs to a family that lives nearby. They must have left the gate open. I will take him back to them. Do you want to come with me?"
Lily and Max nod. They are not scared anymore. They are curious. They pick up their ball and their kite. They follow the park ranger and the dog. They walk to the house where the dog lives. They see a fence and a gate. The gate is open.
"Look," the park ranger says. "This is why the dog got out. Someone forgot to close the gate. We have to be careful with gates. They keep us and our pets safe."
He closes the gate and knocks on the door. A woman opens the door. She is happy to see the dog.
"Oh, thank you, thank you!" she says. "This is Rex. He is our dog. He is very friendly, but he loves to run and chase things. He must have escaped when we were not looking. We are so sorry for the trouble he caused."
She hugs the dog and gives him a treat. She also thanks Lily and Max and the park ranger. She gives them cookies and juice. Lily and Max are happy. They share their cookies and juice with Rex. They play with him and his toys. They make a new friend. They learn to be careful with gates. They have a good day.

Sara and Ben were twins. They liked to play games and have fun. But they did not like to clean their room. They were lazy.
One day, their mom said, "Sara and Ben, you have to clean your room. It is very messy. If you do not clean it, you will not get any cookies." She gave them a key. "This is the key to the cookie jar. I will put it on the table. When you are done, you can get the cookies. But do not lose the key."
Sara and Ben nodded. They did not want to lose the cookies. But they did not want to clean their room either. They had a plan. They decided to order their toys. They put all their toys in a big pile. Then they said, "Toys, clean the room. We are the bosses. You have to do what we say."
But the toys did not move. They did not listen. They were just toys. Sara and Ben waited and waited. But nothing happened. They got bored and sleepy. They forgot about the key and the cookies. They fell asleep on the floor.
Their mom came back. She saw the big pile of toys and the dirty room. She saw Sara and Ben sleeping. She saw the key on the table. She shook her head. She said, "Sara and Ben, you are very silly. You cannot order your toys. You have to do the work yourself. You are too lazy. Now you have no cookies. Maybe next time you will listen to me." She took the key and the cookie jar. She left the room. Sara and Ben did not hear her. They did not get any cookies. They were sad.

Sara and Ben liked to play with their blocks. They liked to make towers and houses and cars. Sometimes they added more blocks to make their towers taller or their houses bigger. They had fun with their blocks.
One day, Sara and Ben decided to make an ambulance with their blocks. They used red and white blocks to make the body and the lights. They used black blocks to make the wheels and the windows. They added a blue block to make the siren. They were proud of their ambulance.
They wanted to play with their ambulance, but they did not have any people to put inside. They looked around and saw their dolls and stuffed animals. They picked some of them and put them in the ambulance. They pretended that the dolls and animals were sick or hurt and needed help.
"Help, help!" Sara said, holding a teddy bear. "My bear has a boo-boo on his paw. He needs to go to the hospital."
"Don't worry, Sara," Ben said, driving the ambulance. "I am a friendly doctor. I will take your bear to the hospital and make him better."
Ben drove the ambulance to the other side of the room, where they had made a hospital with more blocks. He took the teddy bear out of the ambulance and put him on a bed. He looked at his paw and said, "Oh, this is not a big boo-boo. You just need a band-aid."
He took a band-aid from his pocket and put it on the teddy bear's paw. He gave the teddy bear a hug and said, "There, you are all better now. You can go home with Sara."
Sara smiled and hugged her teddy bear. She thanked Ben for being a friendly doctor. She said, "You are the best brother ever. I love you."
They put the teddy bear back in the ambulance and drove back to their blocks. They played with their ambulance and their dolls and animals for a long time. They had fun with their blocks.

Ben and Lily liked to play near the water. They saw big boats that went fast and made loud noises. They saw small boats that had sails and looked like birds. They saw one boat that was very big and had many rooms and windows. It was a yacht. Ben and Lily wanted to see the yacht up close.
They waited until no one was looking and ran to the yacht. They climbed on the ladder and went inside. They saw many interesting things. They saw a big bed, a shiny table, a soft sofa, and a TV. They saw a fridge that had food and drinks. They saw a closet that had clothes and toys. They saw a door that had a sign that said "Do not enter".
Ben and Lily were curious. They wanted to see what was behind the door. They opened the door and saw a dark room. They saw a big machine that made a loud noise. They saw wires and buttons and lights. They saw a sign that said "Danger". They did not know what it meant.
They touched the buttons and the lights. They heard a beep and a click. They saw a red light that flashed. They saw smoke and fire. They smelled something bad. They felt hot and scared. They wanted to get out. They ran to the door but it was locked. They shouted for help but no one heard them. They started to cry and worry. They wished they had not gone to the yacht. They wished they had stayed near the water. They wished they had listened to the signs. They wished they had been good. But it was too late. The yacht exploded and Ben and Lily were gone. The end.

Ben and Sam are friends. They like to play with cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. One day, they find a new car in the park. It is big and shiny and red. Ben and Sam both want the car.
"Let me have it!" Ben says. He tries to take the car from Sam.
"No, it is mine!" Sam says. He holds the car tight.
They pull and tug and shout. They are not happy. They are not friends.
A dog sees them. The dog likes cars too. He runs to them and barks. He jumps and bites the car. He takes the car away from Ben and Sam.
"Hey, stop!" Ben and Sam say. They chase the dog. But the dog is fast and runs away. He has the car.
Ben and Sam are sad. They have no car. They have no fun. They look at each other.
"I am sorry," Ben says. "I was mean. I should have let you have a turn."
"I am sorry too," Sam says. "I was greedy. I should have shared with you."
They hug and smile. They are friends again. They go back to their other cars. They play and take turns. They are happy.
The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. Taking is not nice. Friends are more important than things.

Lily and Ben were on a big train with their mom and dad. They were going to visit their grandma and grandpa in another town. Lily and Ben liked to look out the window and see the trees, the houses, and the animals.
"Look, Ben, a cow!" Lily said, pointing to a black and white cow in a field.
"Moo!" Ben said, making a cow sound.
Mom gave them each a sandwich and a juice box. They were hungry from the long ride.
"Thank you, mom," Lily and Ben said.
They opened their sandwiches and took a bite. Lily chewed her cheese sandwich slowly and carefully. She was thoughtful and did not want to make a mess. Ben chewed his ham sandwich fast and loud. He was excited and did not care about the crumbs.
"Ben, chew quietly, please," mom said. "And don't drop your sandwich on the floor."
"Sorry, mom," Ben said. He tried to chew quieter, but he still dropped some ham on his lap.
Lily giggled. She gave Ben a napkin and helped him clean up.
"You are a good sister, Lily," Ben said.
"You are a good brother, Ben," Lily said.
They smiled and hugged each other. They finished their sandwiches and juice boxes and threw the trash in a bin.
The train stopped at a station. They heard a loud voice say, "This is our stop. Please get off the train with your bags."
"Come on, kids, let's go," dad said. He took their bags and held their hands.
They got off the train and saw their grandma and grandpa waiting for them. They ran to them and gave them big hugs and kisses.
"Hello, Lily and Ben, we are so happy to see you!" grandma and grandpa said.
"We are happy to see you too!" Lily and Ben said.
They all walked to the car and drove to grandma and grandpa's house. They had a fun and happy time together.

Ben is a brown dog who likes to nap. He naps on his soft bed, on the couch, on the rug, and sometimes on his owner's lap. He naps when it is sunny, when it is rainy, when it is quiet, and when it is noisy. He naps a lot.
One day, Ben hears a new sound. It is a loud and fast sound, like a big bee. He looks out the window and sees a yellow car. The car is in motion. It goes up and down the street, and makes a beep-beep noise. Ben is curious. He wants to see the car closer.
He jumps off the couch and runs to the door. He barks and scratches the door. His owner opens the door and lets him out. Ben runs after the car. He tries to catch it, but it is too fast. He runs and runs, but he cannot reach it. He gets tired and hot. He stops and lies down on the grass. He naps.
The car stops too. The driver gets out and sees Ben. He smiles and walks to him. He pets Ben and gives him a treat. He says, "Hello, little dog. You are a good runner. Do you want to ride in my car?" Ben wags his tail and barks. He likes the driver. He likes the treat. He likes the car.
The driver picks up Ben and puts him in the car. He drives him back to his house. He knocks on the door and gives Ben to his owner. He says, "I found your dog chasing my car. He is a brave and friendly dog. I gave him a ride and a snack. He napped in the car. He is a good napper." Ben's owner thanks the driver and hugs Ben. He says, "You are a silly and adventurous dog. I'm glad you are safe and happy. Now let's go inside and nap some more." Ben agrees. He naps.

Tim and Lily were friends. They liked to play with toys. One night, Tim saw a black car in Lily's room. He wanted the car. He said to Lily, "Can I have your car?"
Lily said, "No, this is my car. I got it for my birthday. You have your own car."
Tim was angry. He waited until Lily was asleep. He took the car and ran to his room. He thought he was clever.
But Lily woke up and saw that her car was gone. She cried and called her mom. Her mom came and asked, "What's wrong, Lily?"
Lily said, "Tim stole my car. He took it in the night. He is a bad friend."
Her mom hugged her and said, "Don't worry, Lily. We will get your car back. Stealing is wrong. Tim will be sorry."
Her mom went to Tim's room and knocked on the door. She said, "Tim, open the door. I need to talk to you."
Tim was scared. He knew he did a bad thing. He hid the car under his bed. He said, "What do you want?"
Her mom said, "I want you to give back Lily's car. You stole it from her. That is not nice. How would you feel if someone stole your car?"
Tim felt ashamed. He said, "I'm sorry. I wanted the car. It was black and shiny. I didn't think Lily would miss it."
Her mom said, "Lily loves her car. She was very sad when she saw it was gone. You hurt her feelings. You need to say sorry to her and give her back the car."
Tim took the car and followed her mom to Lily's room. He said to Lily, "I'm sorry, Lily. I stole your car. It was wrong. Here is your car. Can you forgive me?"
Lily looked at Tim and saw that he was sorry. She said, "Thank you, Tim. I forgive you. But don't steal again. It is not nice. We can share our cars if we ask nicely."
Tim nodded and said, "You're right, Lily. I'm sorry. Can we still be friends?"
Lily smiled and said, "Yes, we can still be friends. But next time, ask me first."
They hugged and played with their cars. They learned a lesson. Stealing is bad. Sharing is good. Friends are better.

Tom and Lily were humble mice who lived in a hole under the floor. They liked to find crumbs and cheese in the kitchen, but they had to be careful of the big cat who guarded the house. Sometimes, the cat would chase them and make a loud noise with his claws and teeth.
One day, Tom and Lily were looking for food when they heard the cat coming. They ran back to their hole, but the cat was faster. He blocked their way and hissed at them. "You are my lunch, little mice!" he said.
Tom and Lily were very scared. They looked around for a way to escape. They saw a small gap under the cupboard. "Quick, Lily, follow me!" Tom said. He squeezed through the gap and Lily followed him. The cat tried to reach them, but he was too big. He scratched the cupboard and made a louder noise.
Tom and Lily ran through the gap and found a new hole behind the fridge. They crawled inside and felt safe. They hugged each other and thanked the gap for saving them. "That was a close one, Tom," Lily said. "Yes, it was, Lily," Tom said. "But we are brave and smart, and we stick together. We will always escape the cat." They smiled and cuddled in their new home.

One day, they want to play with a new doll. The doll has long hair and a pink dress. Lily and Ben both want the doll. They start to pull the doll from each other. The doll's hair and dress get torn. Lily and Ben are angry and sad.
They stop playing and sit on the floor. They do not look at each other. They do not sign to each other. They are troubled. They do not know how to say sorry.
Then, their mom comes in. She sees the doll and the children. She is not happy. She signs to them: "What happened? Why did you break the doll? Why are you not playing nicely?"
Lily and Ben look at their mom. They feel ashamed. They sign to their mom: "We are sorry. We both wanted the doll. We fought over the doll. We did not share. We did not listen. We did not use our words."
Their mom nods. She signs to them: "I understand. It is hard to share sometimes. But you have to be kind and respectful. You have to use your words to solve problems. You have to say sorry when you hurt someone. Can you do that?"
Lily and Ben nod. They look at each other. They sign to each other: "I am sorry. I was wrong. I should have shared. I should have listened. I should have used my words. Can we be friends again?"
They hug each other. They smile. They are not troubled anymore. They pick up the doll and fix her hair and dress. They decide to take turns playing with her. They thank their mom for helping them. They go back to playing with their dolls. They make the dolls talk and do things. They use sign language because they can.

Ben and Mia were playing with their toys in the living room. Ben had a big truck and Mia had a doll. They liked to make noises and pretend they were driving or talking.
"Vroom, vroom, my truck is fast and strong!" Ben said.
"My doll is pretty and nice, she likes to sing and dance!" Mia said.
They were having fun, but then Ben saw something on the floor. It was a piece of gum. It was pink and sticky and looked weird.
"Hey, what is this?" Ben asked, picking up the gum.
"Don't touch that, it's yucky!" Mia said. "Mommy said gum is for chewing, not for playing."
But Ben was curious. He wondered what would happen if he attached the gum to something. He looked around and saw Mia's doll. He had an idea.
"Watch this, Mia!" Ben said, and he stuck the gum on the doll's hair.
"Ben, no!" Mia shouted. "You ruined my doll! She has gum in her hair!"
Mia started to cry. Ben realized he had made a mistake. He tried to pull the gum off, but it was too sticky. It made the doll's hair worse.
"I'm sorry, Mia, I'm sorry!" Ben said. "I didn't mean to hurt your doll. I just wanted to see what the gum would do."
Mia was very sad and angry. She didn't want to play with Ben anymore. She ran to Mommy and showed her the doll.
"Mommy, look what Ben did!" Mia said. "He put gum in my doll's hair! He's mean!"
Mommy looked at the doll and the gum. She was not happy. She took the doll and the gum and told Ben to come with her.
"Ben, you know you shouldn't play with gum. It's not a toy. It's dirty and sticky and can make a mess. And you shouldn't attach it to Mia's doll. That was not nice. You hurt her feelings and her doll. You need to say sorry and help me fix it." Mommy said.
Ben felt bad. He knew Mommy was right. He said sorry to Mia and Mommy. He helped Mommy wash the doll's hair and get the gum out. It took a long time and a lot of soap.
Mia watched them. She saw that Ben was sorry and that he tried to help. She felt a little better. She still loved her doll, even with the weird gum hair.
"Thank you, Ben, for helping Mommy. And thank you, Mommy, for fixing my doll." Mia said.
"You're welcome, Mia. And thank you, Ben, for saying sorry and being a good brother." Mommy said.
Ben and Mia hugged each other and Mommy. They learned a lesson. They decided not to play with gum anymore. They went back to their toys and played nicely. They were happy again.

Lily and Tom were on a train with their mom and dad. They were going to visit their grandma and grandpa in another town. The train was very fast and loud, but Lily and Tom were not excited. They were tired and bored.
"Mom, when will we get there?" Lily asked, yawning.
"Soon, honey, soon. Look, there are some cows and sheep outside the window. Can you count them?" Mom said, trying to cheer her up.
Lily looked, but she did not care. She yawned again and closed her eyes. Tom was playing with his toy car, but he was not happy either. He wanted to run and jump and play, not sit still and quiet.
"Dad, can I have a snack?" Tom asked, feeling hungry.
"Sure, buddy, sure. Here, have some crackers and cheese. But be careful, the cheese is a bit bitter. Do you like it?" Dad said, handing him a small bag.
Tom took a bite, but he did not like it. He made a face and spit it out. The cheese was too bitter for him. He wanted something sweet and yummy.
"Yuck, I don't like this cheese. Can I have some candy?" Tom said, whining.
"No, Tom, no. Candy is not good for you. You can have some fruit or yogurt instead. They are sweet and healthy." Dad said, trying to be firm.
Tom did not want fruit or yogurt. He wanted candy. He pouted and threw his toy car on the floor. Lily opened her eyes and saw him. She was annoyed by his noise.
"Tom, stop being a baby. You are too big for candy. And don't throw your toys. You will break them or lose them." Lily said, scolding him.
Tom did not listen to her. He did not like her bossing him around. He stuck his tongue out at her and said, "You are a meanie. You are not my sister. You are a monster."
Lily was hurt by his words. She felt tears in her eyes. She said, "You are a meanie too. You are not my brother. You are a worm."
Mom and Dad heard them fighting. They were not happy. They said, "Lily and Tom, stop it. You are both being rude and silly. You are brother and sister, and you should love each other and share. We are almost at grandma and grandpa's house. They are waiting for you with hugs and cookies. Don't you want to see them and be nice?"
Lily and Tom looked at each other. They felt sorry for what they said. They knew they loved each other and their grandma and grandpa. They said, "Sorry, mom and dad. Sorry, Lily. Sorry, Tom. We will be nice and share. We want to see grandma and grandpa and have hugs and cookies."
Mom and Dad smiled and hugged them. They said, "That's good. We love you both. Now, look, the train is slowing down. We are here. Let's get ready to go."
Lily and Tom grabbed their bags and toys. They were not tired and bored anymore. They were excited and happy. They got off the train and ran to their grandma and grandpa, who were waving and smiling. They gave them big hugs and kisses. They said, "Hi, grandma and grandpa. We missed you. We love you."
Grandma and grandpa said, "Hi, Lily and Tom. We missed you too. We love you. Come on, let's go inside. We have cookies and milk for you. And some candy too, but only a little bit."
Lily and Tom smiled and followed them. They were glad they came. They knew they would have a lot of fun and learn a lot of things. They forgot about the bitter cheese and the loud train. They only remembered the sweet cookies and the warm hugs.

Tim and Sam were playing with their toy soldiers in the yard. They liked to pretend they were in a big war and make loud noises. Tim had a red soldier and Sam had a blue soldier. They said the red soldier was the good guy and the blue soldier was the bad guy.
"Bang! Bang! You are dead, blue soldier!" Tim shouted, throwing his red soldier at Sam's blue soldier.
"No, I am not! You missed, red soldier!" Sam shouted back, dodging the red soldier and throwing his blue soldier at Tim's head.
"Ow! That hurt, Sam! You are stupid!" Tim cried, rubbing his head and picking up his red soldier.
"I am not stupid, Tim! You are stupid!" Sam said, picking up his blue soldier and running away.
Tim chased Sam around the yard, trying to hit him with his red soldier. Sam ran faster and faster, until he reached the fence. He saw a big dog on the other side of the fence, barking and growling. Sam was scared of the dog. He stopped and turned around.
"Help, Tim! There is a dog!" Sam yelled, holding his blue soldier in front of him.
Tim saw the dog too. He was also scared of the dog. He ran to Sam and stood next to him.
"Maybe the dog will go away if we are quiet," Tim whispered, holding his red soldier in his hand.
The dog did not go away. It jumped on the fence and tried to bite them. Tim and Sam screamed and threw their soldiers at the dog. The dog caught the soldiers in its mouth and ran away.
"Hey, come back, dog! Those are our soldiers!" Tim and Sam shouted, running after the dog.
But the dog was too fast for them. It disappeared behind a house. Tim and Sam stopped and looked at each other. They had no soldiers left.
"I am sorry, Tim. I did not mean to hurt you with my blue soldier," Sam said, feeling sad.
"I am sorry, Sam. I did not mean to call you stupid with my red soldier," Tim said, feeling sorry.
They hugged and said they were friends again. They decided to go back to the yard and find something else to play with. They learned that war was not fun and that they should yield to each other. They also learned that dogs liked to eat soldiers.

Tom and Sam are brothers. They share a room. Tom likes to keep his toys tidy. Sam likes to make a mess. One day, Tom sees that his favorite car is missing. He looks under the bed, in the closet, and in the drawers. He cannot find it.
He goes to Sam and asks, "Sam, did you take my car?"
Sam shakes his head and says, "No, I did not. I do not like your car. It is too small and red."
Tom does not believe him. He thinks Sam is a thief and a liar. He says, "You are a thief and a liar. You took my car and hid it somewhere. Give it back to me now!"
Sam gets angry and says, "I am not a thief and a liar. You are a mean and bossy brother. Go away and leave me alone!"
They start to fight and push each other. Their mom hears the noise and comes to their room. She sees the mess and the boys fighting. She is not happy. She says, "Stop it, both of you! What is going on here?"

"Maybe it is sleepy," Mira said. "Look, it is yawning."
Mira and Sam watched as the worm opened and closed its mouth. They thought it looked like a yawn. They did not know that worms do not yawn. They just breathe through their skin.
"Maybe we should let it go back to the soil," Mira said. "It might be happier there."
"Okay, Mira, let's do that," Sam said. "Bye, worm, have a good nap."
They gently put the worm back in the hole they dug and covered it with soil. Then they waved and said goodbye. They felt happy that they made a new friend. They did not know that the worm did not care. It just wanted to eat and hide.

So they did, they danced together until the stars twinkled in the night sky. And Teddy soon forgot all about the frog and the slap. He had so much fun dancing with the rabbit.

The pine tree said, "I do not know, but if we unite and search together, we will find the bird's home." So, Lily and the pine tree searched together and found the bird's home. The bird was very happy and thanked them both.
The moral of the story is that when we unite and work together, we can accomplish great things.

Every Saturday, Henry would take his mule to the market to supply things to the people. Henry was a serious worker, always doing his best to make sure his customers got what they wanted.
One sunny Saturday, Henry stopped by Mrs. Tom's stand. She had been a regular customer of Henry's for many years.
Mrs. Tom smiled at him. She said, "Henry, I need some apples for my son. Can you supply me with some?"
Henry patted his mule's head. "Of course I can, Mrs. Tom," he said. He lifted a basket full of red apples off of the mule and handed it to Mrs. Tom.
She thanked him and handed him some coins. "You run a serious business, Henry," she said.
Henry nodded, tipping his hat. "Yes, I take this job very serious," he said. He thanked Mrs. Tom and continued on his way.

The moral of this story is that with enough hard work and dedication, you can achieve your goals too, no matter how clumsy you are.

He ran after it as fast as he could, jumping and laughing with joy. After a while, tired from the chase, he stopped to take a break. Suddenly, the spark came up to the boy and started talking to him. 
"You must go back home," said the spark. "It's not safe here. You should not stay here in the dark".
But the boy enjoyed running around and was too excited to listen. He chased the spark further and deeper into the night. Suddenly, everything went dark and the air turned gloomy. 
The boy started to cry as he realized that he has been tricked. The spark had been a bad spirit who was trying to lure him further away from safety. The boy cried and cried until he was finally rescued.
The boy learned a lesson to never go chasing after strange sparks. He remembered it his whole life and was never as happy as he was before.

Once upon a time there was a little fish. He was so happy to swim in the pond. One day, he swam further away from his pond than usual and he saw a big bowl with clear, tasty water. He wanted to take a dip and he quickly jumped in.
The fish was so excited to be swimming in the bowl of tasty water that he stayed in for a very long time. He was having so much fun splashing around that he did not realise that the water was slowly soaking into his skin. 
Suddenly the bowl started to get smaller and smaller. The fish tried to jump out, but he couldn’t. He was stuck! He cried out, “Help me! Please help me!”
Desperate, the fish shouted to his friends in the pond, “Do not jump in the bowl! Stay in the pond!”
The fish’s friends listened and stayed away. Sadly, the bowl shrunk so much that the poor fish died.
This story’s moral is important: always listen to your friends’ advice, even though it might seem fun not to.

When he reached the other side, he saw something he had never seen before: a herd of elephants! He was so happy to come across them and he joined their pack. He walked with them for days and days and had lots of fun.
At the end of his journey, the little elephant returned home with lots of stories to tell. He had learned so much and made lots of new friends!

So the brave and humble lizard decided to do something. He would try to make peace between the frog and his friends. He found the frog and talked to him. He explained why fighting was not good, and how it made everyone unhappy.
The frog heard the wise words of the humble lizard and agreed. He stopped picking fights with the other animals and became friends with them. Everyone was so happy!
From that day, the humble lizard was known as the peacemaker. The animals of the woods went to him whenever they needed help to stay peaceful. He was a very special lizard indeed!

The leopard thought for a bit and then shouted, “I will jump over you!” He then went to the edge of a cliff and jumped.
But the dragon opened its eyes in time and blew a hot and fiery breath. The leopard fell down and hit the ground with a loud thud.
The dragon laughed and flew off into the sky. The brave leopard was never seen again.

"What's wrong? Why are you scared?" his dad asked.
"There's a flood," replied Tom.
His dad smiled. "Don't worry, it's not a bad flood. We'll stay safe inside, but feel free to look out of the window and watch."
Tom ran to the window, looking at the smooth water rising up around their house. But, he was excited by the sight and wasn't scared anymore.

Once there was a little puppy called Brownie who liked to play all day. One day, Brownie saw a nap in the garden, but when he tried to take it, he struggled. Brownie thought he was strong enough, but the nap wouldn't move. 
Brownie growled, “Why won't it move?”
Just then, her big brother, Golden, came running over. He smiled and said, “It's okay, little sis, I'll help you.” He grabbed the nap, and to Brownie's surprise, it came right up. 
Brownie laughed, “That was easy! What's so special about it?”
Golden nodded, “This nap is harmless, and it's not meant to be taken away. That's why you struggled." 
The moral of the story is that if something looks harmless, we should still respect it and not take it away without permission.

"Oh no!" thought Anna. "What was that noise?"
Anna was scared, so she decided to take a closer look. She peered around the corner, and saw a big, brightly coloured bird.
"Hello!" said the bird. "Don't be scared, I'm friendly!"
Anna smiled and said "Hi bird! What are you doing here?"
"I'm looking for something to eat," the bird replied. "Do you have something for me?"
Anna was happy to help. She reached into her backpack and pulled out a tasty snack.
"Here you go!" said Anna, as she handed the snack to the bird.
The bird thanked Anna and flew away. Anna watched as it flew off, feeling happy and not scared anymore.

Jack stepped away. "Am I in trouble, Mommy?" He asked.

Once upon a time Bob and Kate went for a walk in the park. Bob was wearing shoes made of leather and Kate was wearing her favourite dress. As they were walking, Bob saw a little bird in the tree. "What kind of bird is that?" asked Bob.
Kate smiled and explained, "It's a sparrow. It has a brown coat and a black beak." 
Bob's eyes widened. He asked, "Can I hold it?". 
Kate said, "No, you can't, but you can be very polite and just watch it. Maybe it will come closer if you're gentle."
 
Bob nodded and tried to stay very still. Sure enough, the little sparrow flew into his hands and landed on the leather shoes. He held it very gently and the bird didn't try to fly away. Bob smiled, amazed that he was able to hold a real bird.
As Bob and Kate continued their walk, they felt very proud of how polite and gentle Bob had been. They had both learned a valuable lesson about kindness and respect for animals.

Lilly smiled. "That must have been fun. What was the joke?"
Jack giggled. "I asked them, why did the chicken cross the playground? And then I said, to get to the other slide!"
Lilly and Jack cracked up laughing. Lily suddenly looked worried.
"What's the matter, Lilly?" asked Jack.
"I'm starting to get thirsty, Jack. Let's find some water to drink."
"Good idea!" said Jack. "Let's look for some water."
The two friends went looking for some water in the park. In the end, they found a fountain and filled their water bottles up. Lilly and Jack smiled, relieved to have found the water. 
The two of them laughed and joked as they walked back home.

Tom jumps out of bed and puts on his clothes. He brushes his teeth and combs his hair. He packs his bag and goes to the kitchen. He eats his breakfast and says, "Thank you, mom. I'm ready to go."
Sam stays in bed and says, "I don't want to go to school. I want to play." He covers his head with his blanket and closes his eyes. He ignores his mom and the clock.

Maybe I should have hurried." He gets out of bed and puts on his clothes. He brushes his teeth and combs his hair. He packs his bag and goes to the kitchen. He sees his mom and says, "Mom, I'm sorry. He sees the trees and the flowers. He sees the birds and the bugs. He thinks, "This is not fun. This is boring. I wish I was on the bus with Tom and my friends. I wish I was at school with them. I wish I had hurried."
The moral of the story is: You should listen to your mom and hurry when she tells you to. School is good for you and fun. You should not waste your time and miss your chance. You should be a good brother and a good friend. You should be a good boy.

"Pass me the ball, Ben!" Anna shouted.
"OK, Anna!" Ben said. He threw the ball to Anna, but the wind blew it over her head. The ball went over the fence and into the street.
"Oh no!" Anna and Ben said. They ran to the fence and looked for the ball. They saw it on the other side of the street, near a big car. They were fearful. The street was busy and noisy. They knew they should not cross the street without a grown-up.
"What do we do?" Anna asked.

One day, Ben and Max meet a girl and her dog in the park. The girl is wearing a pink dress and a bow in her hair. Her dog is small and white and has a pink collar. The girl says her name is Lily and her dog is Fluffy.
"Hello, I'm Ben and this is Max," Ben says.
"Hello, I'm Lily and this is Fluffy," the girl says.
"Can we play together?" Ben asks.
"Sure, but only if you follow my rules," Lily says.
"What rules?" Ben asks.
"Well, first, you have to say that Fluffy is the most beautiful dog in the world," Lily says.
Ben looks at Fluffy and then at Max. He thinks Max is much more beautiful than Fluffy. He does not want to lie.
"No, I can't say that. Max is the most beautiful dog in the world," Ben says.
Lily gets angry. She says, "No, Fluffy is the most beautiful dog in the world. You are wrong and mean. We can't play with you. Come on, Fluffy, let's go."
She takes Fluffy and walks away. Ben feels sad. He does not understand why Lily is so bossy and rude. He hugs Max and says, "Don't worry, Max, you are the most beautiful dog in the world to me. And you are also the best friend in the world. I love you, Max."
Max wags his tail and licks Ben's face. He does not care about Lily or Fluffy. He is happy to be with Ben. He bows his head and says, "Woof, woof, I love you too, Ben."

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to eat jam on toast. One day, their mom took them to the store to buy some groceries. She told them to stay close to her and not to touch anything.
But Tom and Lily saw a big jar of jam on a shelf. It looked so yummy and red. They wanted to taste it. They looked around and saw that their mom was busy talking to a lady. They thought she would not notice if they took a little bit of jam.
They climbed on a chair and reached for the jar. They opened it and dipped their fingers in it. They licked the jam and smiled. It was so sweet and sticky. They wanted more. They took some more jam and put it in their mouths.
But then they heard their mom's voice. She was calling them. She had finished talking to the lady and was looking for them. Tom and Lily felt scared. They knew they had done something bad. They tried to close the jar and put it back on the shelf. But they were too late. Their mom saw them with jam on their fingers and faces.
"Tom! Lily! What are you doing?" she asked. She was angry and sad. She took the jar from them and looked at the label. It said "Strawberry Jam - $5.99". She had to pay for it.
She took them to the cashier and paid for the jam. She also said sorry to the store owner. She was very ashamed of her children. She took them to the car and drove home.
She did not talk to them on the way. Tom and Lily felt guilty. They knew they had made a big mistake. They had stolen jam from the store. They had lied to their mom. They had wasted money. They had broken a rule.
When they got home, their mom told them to go to their room. She said they had to think about what they had done. She said they had to say sorry to her and to the store owner. She said they had to do some chores to earn back the money. She said they had to learn to be honest and respectful.
Tom and Lily nodded. They went to their room. They felt sorry for what they had done. They hugged each other and cried. They decided to never steal jam again. They decided to always listen to their mom. They decided to be good children.
The moral of the story is: stealing is wrong and hurts others. Honesty and respect are important values. Listening to your parents is a good thing.

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the park every day. They liked to swing, slide and run. One day, they saw a big duck pond in the park. They wanted to feed the ducks.
Lily had some bread in her bag. She broke it into small pieces and threw them to the ducks. The ducks came closer and quacked. Lily was happy. She gave some bread to Ben and said, "Here, you feed them too."
Ben took the bread and threw it to the ducks. But he threw it too hard. One piece hit a duck on the head. The duck was angry. It flapped its wings and chased Ben. Ben was scared. He ran away from the duck. He dropped the bread and bumped into Lily. Lily fell down and hurt her knee. She cried.
Ben felt bad. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I didn't mean to hurt you or the duck. Are you okay?"
Lily looked at her knee. It was red and sore. She looked at Ben. He looked sad and sorry. She looked at the duck. It was graceful and calm. It had stopped chasing Ben and was eating the bread. Lily thought for a moment. She said, "It's okay, Ben. I forgive you. You didn't do it on purpose. And the duck is fine too. See, it's happy now."
Ben smiled. He said, "Thank you, Lily. You're a good friend. Can I help you up?"
Lily nodded. She said, "Yes, please. And can we still play in the park?"
Ben said, "Of course. Let's go to the swings. They're fun and safe."
Lily and Ben held hands and walked to the swings. They forgot about the duck and the bread. They laughed and played. They were best friends again.

Ben and Lily were playing in the park with their toy cars. They liked to zoom them around the grass and make loud noises. Ben had a red car and Lily had a blue car. They were having fun until Ben saw a big hill of dirt.
"Look, Lily, a mountain!" Ben said. "Let's drive our cars up the mountain and see what's on the other side."
Lily looked at the hill and shook her head. "No, Ben, that's not a mountain. That's a tip. It's where people put their rubbish. It's dirty and smelly and there might be bugs or rats. We can't play there."
But Ben didn't listen. He liked the idea of climbing the tip with his car. He thought it would be an adventure. He insisted that Lily should come with him.
"Come on, Lily, don't be scared. It's harmless. It's just dirt and rubbish. Maybe we'll find something cool or shiny. Please, please, please, let's go."
Lily didn't want to go. She didn't like the tip. She thought it was gross and dangerous. She tried to stop Ben from going.
"Ben, no, stop. You can't go there. It's not safe. You might get hurt or sick. Please, please, please, stay with me."
But Ben didn't stop. He pushed his car up the tip, leaving Lily behind. He was curious and excited. He wanted to see what was on the other side.
He soon regretted his decision. As he reached the top of the tip, he saw a big, black, furry thing with sharp teeth and claws. It was a bear. It had smelled the rubbish and came to look for food. It saw Ben and his car and growled.
Ben was terrified. He screamed and dropped his car. He turned around and ran down the tip as fast as he could. He wished he had listened to Lily.
Lily heard Ben's scream and saw him running. She also saw the bear. She was scared too, but she wanted to help Ben. She picked up a stick and waved it at the bear. She shouted and threw stones at it. She hoped it would go away.
The bear was annoyed by Lily's stick and stones. It decided that Ben and his car were not worth the trouble. It snorted and walked away, looking for an easier snack.
Ben reached the bottom of the tip and hugged Lily. He was shaking and crying. He was sorry for being stubborn and foolish. He thanked Lily for saving him.
"I'm sorry, Lily, you were right. The tip was not a mountain. It was not harmless. It was scary and bad. I should have listened to you. You are a good friend. Thank you for helping me."
Lily hugged Ben back. She was glad he was safe. She forgave him for being silly. She was a good friend too.
"It's okay, Ben, I'm glad you're okay. The tip was not a place to play. It was a place to avoid. You learned your lesson. Next time, let's stay on the grass. It's much more fun."

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play in the forest. They had a favorite tree, a big pine, where they built a fort with sticks and leaves. They felt safe and happy in their fort.
One day, a storm came and the wind was very strong. It made loud noises and shook the trees. Ben and Lily ran to their fort to hide. They saw that the pine was bending and cracking. They were scared that it would fall and break their fort.
"Ben, what if the pine falls?" Lily asked, worry in her voice.
"I don't know, Lily. Maybe we should go home and wait for the storm to stop," Ben said, worry in his voice too.
"But I don't want to leave our fort. It's our special place," Lily said, holding on to the pine.
Ben looked at his sister and saw that she loved the pine as much as he did. He loved his sister more than the pine. He decided to be brave and normal.
"Lily, it's okay. We can always make another fort. But we can't make another you or me. Come on, let's go home. Mom and dad will be worry too," Ben said, holding his sister's hand.
Lily nodded and let go of the pine. She trusted her brother and followed him. They ran home and hugged their mom and dad. They told them about the pine and the fort.
Mom and dad smiled and praised them for being smart and caring. They said that the pine was strong and would survive the storm. They said that the fort was fun and creative, but not as important as their safety and love.
Ben and Lily learned that sometimes they had to let go of things they liked to protect things they loved. They learned that worry was normal, but they could overcome it with courage and trust. They learned that the forest was a wonderful place to play, but home was a wonderful place to stay.

Ben thinks this is a fun game. He says, "OK, let's play marry. You look pretty in the blanket. I will give you a ring made of grass." He puts the ring on Sara's finger and says, "I do."
They hug and pretend to kiss. They are very happy.
But Tom, who lives next door, is not happy. He is jealous. He likes Sara too. He wants to play with her. He does not like Ben. He thinks Ben is silly. He says to himself, "I will stop their marry game. I will take the blanket away."
He runs to the garden and grabs the blanket from Sara. He says, "Ha ha, this is my blanket now. You can't play marry anymore. Sara, come and play with me. Ben is boring."
Sara and Ben are very sad and angry. They say to Tom, "No, this is our blanket. You are mean. Go away. We don't want to play with you. We want to play marry."
They try to get the blanket back from Tom. They pull and tug and shout. The blanket rips in half. They all cry.
Mom hears the noise and comes to the garden. She sees the ripped blanket and the crying children. She says, "What happened here? Why are you fighting? Why did you ruin the blanket?"
Sara and Ben tell Mom about their marry game and how Tom took the blanket away. Tom says he was jealous and wanted to play with Sara. Mom says, "That was not nice, Tom. You should not take things that are not yours. You should not ruin other people's games. You should say sorry to Sara and Ben."
Tom feels sorry. He says, "I'm sorry, Sara and Ben. I was jealous. I like Sara too. Can we be friends?"
Sara and Ben forgive Tom. They say, "It's OK, Tom. We can be friends. But you have to share and be nice. And you can't play marry with us. That's our game."
Mom says, "That's very good, children. You can be friends and play together. But you have to be careful with the blanket. It's old and fragile. It was my grandma's blanket. She gave it to me when I was little. It's very special to me."
She hugs the children and gives them each a piece of the blanket. She says, "You can keep these as a souvenir of your marry game. But don't rip them anymore. And remember, you are too young to marry. You have to grow up first."
The children nod and smile. They say, "We know, Mom. We were just playing. We love you."
They hug Mom and each other. They are happy again.

Sam and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they find a big sack near a tree. It is black and heavy.
"Look, a sack!" Sam says. "What is inside?"
"I don't know. Let's open it!" Mia says. They pull the sack to a bench and open it.
Inside, they see many shiny things. There are rings, necklaces, bracelets, and earrings. They are all gold and silver and have jewels on them.
"Wow, so pretty!" Mia says. She picks up a necklace with a big red jewel. She puts it around her neck.
"Look, I'm a princess!" she says.
Sam sees a bow and an arrow. They are also gold and have jewels on them.
"Look, I'm a hunter!" he says. He picks up the bow and the arrow. He aims at a bird on a branch.
"Sam, no!" Mia says. "Don't hurt the bird!"
But Sam does not listen. He shoots the arrow. It flies in the air and hits the bird. The bird falls to the ground.
"Sam, you are bad!" Mia says. She runs to the bird. It is not moving. It has blood on its feathers.
"Sorry, Mia. I didn't mean to." Sam says. He drops the bow and the arrow. He follows Mia.
They see a man running towards them. He is angry. He has a mask on his face. He is the thief who stole the sack from the shop.
"Hey, you kids! Give me back my sack!" he says. He grabs the sack from the bench. He pushes Sam and Mia away.
"Help, help!" Sam and Mia shout. They are scared.
A policeman hears them. He sees the thief with the sack. He runs after him. He catches him and puts handcuffs on him.
"Thank you, officer!" Sam and Mia say. They hug the policeman.
"You're welcome, kids. You did the right thing. This man is a bad man. He took these things from the shop. They are not his. They belong to the people who made them and sold them." the policeman says.
He takes the thief and the sack to his car. He drives away.
Sam and Mia look at the bird. It is still not moving.
"Is the bird dead?" Sam asks.
"I think so." Mia says. She is sad.
They bury the bird under the tree. They say sorry to the bird.
They go home. They tell their parents what happened. Their parents hug them and say they are proud of them.
They learn a lesson. They do not play with things that are not theirs. They do not hurt animals. They are good friends.

Mary felt so much better, like a heavy weight had been lifted off her shoulders. As a surprise her mom asked her to get in the car and took her to the gas station.
Mary was so excited and couldn't believe it. As Mary walked into the gas station, she found something special - a big box of chocolates!
Mary was so glad her mom had forgiven her and had given her something special as well. She thanked her mom and promised that she would never make the same mistake again.
Mary learned a valuable lesson that day - that it was important to forgive and forget. From then onwards, she would always try her best to use kind words whenever she was feeling nervous.

One day, he was sitting with his mum and playing with the spoon. Suddenly, he felt a big strike on his shoulder. He turned around and saw his mum with a stern look on her face.

The boy looked down at the spoon in his hand and realised he had been striking it all along. He apologised to mum and put the spoon down on the table.
From then on, the boy ate his soup without striking the spoon. But sometimes, when mum wasn't looking, he couldn't help but strike the spoon with a little smile.

Without thinking, Tom ran towards the butterfly. Suddenly, the butterfly started to fly away. Tom was so sad, he wanted to hold it in his hands.
But then the big yellow butterfly stopped and it seemed to fly lower and nearer to the ground. Then it began to slowly flutter down to the ground and landed right next to Tom. Tom was so excited! Now he could get closer to look at the butterfly up close. He looked around and then slowly yielded his hand to touch the butterfly and it stayed still. Tom smiled with excitement. He felt so lucky to be able to get so close to such a beautiful creature!
Tom was so happy with this special moment. He stood there, smiling and looking at the big yellow butterfly with its shiny green wings. It was the most beautiful thing he had ever seen!

One day, she worked up her courage and decided to dare herself to have a look. She took a deep breath, then stepped onto the prickly hedge. She tried not to make any silly noises as she looked around.
But then, all of a sudden, something came out of the darkness. It was a big, white rabbit! The little girl was so frightened she jumped off the hedge and ran back to her house.
The next day, she was back again, wanting to find out more about the mysterious hedge. But this time, she brought a friend with her to make her feel safer. Together, they slowly stepped onto the hedge and looked around. Nothing came out this time, so they both shouted "Boo!" just for fun.
It turns out the hedge was never dangerous, it was just a bit silly! From then on, the little girl was always brave enough to explore the hedge with her friend.

Confused, Kim asked, "How does the clock know?" Her mom said that there were numbers on the clock and the numbers tell you if it's morning, afternoon, or night.
Kim thought about this for a minute and asked another funny question, "Do the numbers move?". Mom said yes, that the numbers were like a boat on the sea and when the sea moved the boat moved too. Kim asked, "Do I move the clock?" and her mom said no, the hour and minute hands took care of it.
Kim thought this was really funny and had to tell her friends all about it! She was very proud of her new knowledge about the clock.

Foxy went up to Bunny and said, "Hello Bunny, that carrot looks delicious. Can I have a bite?" Bunny replied, "No, this is my carrot. You can't have any." Foxy thought for a moment and said, "I have an idea. Let's play a game. If I can guess what's inside that carrot, you have to give it to me."
Bunny agreed to the game and Foxy guessed that there was a diamond inside the carrot. Bunny laughed and said, "No silly, carrots don't have diamonds inside them!" Foxy replied, "I know that, I was just joking. But now that we're playing a game, let me guess again. I think the carrot will melt in the sun if we leave it out for too long."
Bunny was surprised and said, "Wow, you're very clever Foxy. I didn't know that." Foxy smiled and said, "Thank you Bunny, but now you have to give me the carrot since I won the game." Bunny laughed and gave Foxy the carrot, knowing that Foxy had tricked him once again.

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big slide. Sara wants to go first. She climbs up the ladder and sits on the slide. She is happy.
"Look at me, Tom!" she says. "I am going to slide down fast!"
But Sara slides too fast. She does not hold on to the slide. She falls off the slide and lands on the grass. She hurts her knee. It bleeds. She cries.
"Ow, ow, ow!" she says. "My knee hurts!"
Tom runs to Sara. He is worried. He sees her knee. He wants to help her.
"Don't cry, Sara," he says. "I have something for you."
He takes out a grape from his pocket. He gives it to Sara.
"Here, Sara," he says. "Eat this grape. It is sweet and juicy. It will make you feel better."
Sara takes the grape. She bites it. It is sweet and juicy. She likes it. She stops crying.
"Thank you, Tom," she says. "The grape is good. But my knee still hurts."
Tom thinks. He remembers what his mom told him. He has an idea.
"I know what to do, Sara," he says. "We need to heal your knee. We need to put something on it. Something flexible and soft. Something like this."
He takes out a band-aid from his pocket. He opens it. He sticks it on Sara's knee.
"There, Sara," he says. "Now your knee has a band-aid. It will protect your knee. It will help your knee heal. It is flexible and soft. You can bend your knee. See?"
Sara bends her knee. She feels the band-aid. It is flexible and soft. It does not hurt. She smiles.
"Wow, Tom," she says. "You are smart. The band-aid is good. It makes my knee feel better. Thank you, Tom. You are a good friend."
Tom smiles too. He is happy. He hugs Sara.
"You are welcome, Sara," he says. "You are a good friend too. Come on, let's play some more. But be careful on the slide, okay?"
Sara nods. She holds Tom's hand. They go to play some more. They are happy. They are friends.

As she was picking some carrots, she noticed a little bunny hopping around. The bunny was so cute and Mrs. Smith wanted to pet it. But the bunny was scared and ran away. Mrs. Smith didn't want to scare the bunny, so she left it alone and went back to her kitchen to bake some carrot cake. 
Later that day, Mrs. Smith brought the cake to her neighbor's house. The neighbor was so happy and said it was the best cake she had ever tasted. Mrs. Smith felt proud and happy that she could make someone else smile. From that day on, Mrs. Smith always made sure to pick extra vegetables for her neighbors and share her delicious treats.

Ben was a bald boy who liked to play outside. He had no hair on his head, but he had a big smile on his face. He did not care what other kids said about him. He was happy and kind.
One day, he saw a white feather on the ground. He picked it up and wondered where it came from. He looked up and saw a bright light in the sky. He thought it was an angel. He wanted to see the angel, so he started to follow the light.
He ran and ran, but the light was too fast. He did not see where he was going. He crossed the street without looking. A car was coming and honked its horn. Ben was scared and stopped. The car stopped too, just in time.
The driver got out of the car and checked on Ben. He was angry and said, "What are you doing, kid? You could have been hurt! You should not follow things you do not know. You should be careful and listen to your parents."
Ben was sorry and said, "I'm sorry, sir. I saw a feather and a light. I thought it was an angel. I wanted to see the angel."
The driver looked at the feather and the light. He realized that the light was a plane and the feather was from a bird. He felt sorry for Ben and said, "I'm sorry, too, kid. I did not mean to yell at you. There is no angel here, just a plane and a bird. But you know what? You are an angel. You are an angel because you are brave and good. You do not need hair to be beautiful. You have a heart that shines."
Ben smiled and said, "Thank you, sir. You are nice. Can I keep the feather?"
The driver nodded and said, "Sure, kid. You can keep the feather. It is a gift from the bird. But remember, do not follow things you do not know. Follow your heart and your dreams. They will lead you to the real angels."
Ben hugged the driver and said, "Thank you, sir. I will remember. Goodbye."
Ben went back to his home and showed his parents the feather. He told them what happened and what the driver said. His parents were proud of him and hugged him. They said, "We love you, Ben. You are our angel. You make us happy every day."
Ben was happy too. He put the feather in his room and looked at it. He thought of the driver and the bird. He thought of the angels. He closed his eyes and said, "Thank you, angels. Thank you for watching over me."

"Can we play in the park later?" Ben asks.
"Maybe, if we have time," mom says.
They ride the bus for a long time. They get off the bus. They walk to grandma's house. They see the house. It is white and tall. It has a red door and a blue roof. It has many stairs.
"Wow, grandma's house is so big!" Anna says.
"Yes, it is. Do you remember how to climb the stairs?" mom asks.
"Yes, we do. We hold the railing and we count the stairs," Ben says.
They climb the stairs. They count the stairs. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten. They reach the door. They knock on the door. They hear grandma's voice.
"Who is it?" grandma asks.
"It's us, grandma. Anna and Ben and mom," Anna says.

She opens the door. She hugs them. She has a big smile and thick glasses. She smells like cookies and flowers.
"Hello, grandma. We missed you," Ben says.
"Hello, my darlings. I missed you too. Come in, come in. I have something for you," grandma says.

"You're welcome, my dears. You are so sweet. Now, let's have some fun," grandma says.

Sara and Tom were playing hide and seek in the park. Sara was the seeker and Tom was the hider. Sara counted to ten and then opened her eyes. She looked around and saw a big sack near a tree. She thought Tom might be hiding inside it.
She ran to the sack and lifted it up. But there was no Tom inside, only some leaves and sticks. She was puzzled. Where did Tom go? She called out, "Tom, where are you? I can't find you!"
Tom heard Sara's voice from a distant bush. He giggled and whispered, "She can't see me. I'm a good hider. I made the sack look like me and then I ran away. I'm going to vanish like a ghost."
He waited for Sara to come closer and then he jumped out of the bush and shouted, "Boo!" Sara was startled and screamed. Then she laughed and said, "You scared me, Tom! You're a tricky hider. How did you make the sack look like you?"
Tom showed Sara how he put his hat and jacket on the sack and stuffed it with leaves and sticks. He said, "It was easy. I just used what I found in the park. Do you want to try it too?"
Sara nodded and said, "Yes, let's do it again. But this time, I'll be the hider and you'll be the seeker. And I'll vanish better than you!"
They put the sack back on the ground and swapped their roles. They had fun playing hide and seek with the sack until it was time to go home.

But then the sun came out and it became very warm. The snow started to melt and drip. Anna and Ben saw their snowman getting smaller and smaller. They were very sad and scared.
"Mommy, mommy, our snowman is going away!" they cried and ran to their mother, who was sitting on a bench.
"Don't worry, my loves, it's just the snow melting. It happens when it gets warm. Your snowman is not going away, he is just changing into water. You can still play with the water and make bubbles and splashes," their mother said and hugged them.
"But we want our snowman back! He was our friend! He will be lonely without us!" Anna and Ben said and sniffed.
Suddenly, they heard a loud noise in the sky. It was thunder. They looked up and saw dark clouds and flashes of light. They felt drops of rain on their faces.
"Look, my loves, the rain is coming. The rain is the water that comes from the clouds. The clouds are made of water too, just like your snowman. Maybe your snowman is going to the clouds to make more snow for another day. Maybe he is not lonely, maybe he is having fun with other snowmen in the sky," their mother said and smiled.
Anna and Ben looked at the sky and imagined their snowman flying with the clouds. They felt a little better and smiled too.
"Maybe you are right, mommy. Maybe our snowman is happy in the sky. Maybe we will see him again when it snows. Can we make another snowman then?" they asked.
"Of course, my loves, we can make another snowman then. And we can give him a different hat, a different scarf and a different nose. We can make him as big and as beautiful as we want. And we can play with him and be his friends. But for now, let's go home and have some hot chocolate. It's getting cold and wet," their mother said and took their hands.
Anna and Ben nodded and followed their mother. They said goodbye to their snowman in the sky and thanked him for the fun they had. They hoped he would come back soon. They were not so sad and scared anymore. They were still happy and proud of their snowman.

"But I want to be its friend. Can we give it some mail?" Tom asks.
His dad laughs. "Mail is for people, not for animals. The fox doesn't need mail. It needs food and water and a safe place to live."
Tom is sad. He likes mail and thinks the fox would like it too. He looks at the mail in his hands. He sees a package that is small and round and has a picture of a ball on it. He thinks the fox would like to play with the ball.
"Dad, can I deliver this package to the fox?" Tom asks.
His dad looks at the package. He sees that it is for a house that is very far away. He knows that Tom likes to deliver mail, but he also knows that they have to follow the rules.
"Sorry, Tom, but we can't do that. This package belongs to someone else. We have to deliver it to the right address. That's our job," his dad says.
Tom is disappointed. He wants to make the fox happy, but he also wants to do his job well. He puts the package back in the truck and looks out the window. He sees the fox again, hiding behind a tree. The fox looks at him with curious eyes.
Tom smiles and waves at the fox. The fox wags its tail and runs away. Tom feels a little better. He thinks that maybe the fox is not so lonely after all. He thinks that maybe the fox has other friends in the woods. He thinks that maybe he can see the fox again someday.
He turns to his dad and says, "Dad, I'm ready to deliver more mail. Let's go."

Lila looks at the map and sees that it has some pictures and words on it. She tries to read them, but they are too hard for her. She only knows some letters and sounds.
"I don't know, Ben. The map has some things I can't read. Maybe we can ask Mom or Dad to help us."

This made the bunny angry. He hopped over to the fish and yelled again, "Move, fish!" The fish said nothing and kept swimming in circles. Seeing the fish wouldn't move, the bunny got angry and said, "If you don't move, I'll bite your tooth!"

So, the bunny and the fish both had a drink and the bunny moved back to his own side of the pond. From that day forward, the bunny was always kind, helpful and generous. He had learned his lesson—being fancy isn't nearly as important as being kind.

Ella started pushing the spoon too. They both pushed the spoon around the bowl and laughed together. Then Mama said, "Look Ella, the spoon is breaking the rice!"
Ella was surprised and said, "What does the broken rice do, mama?"
Mama said, "It helps make the cake sweet. Now we can put the broken rice in the cake and it will taste yummy when it's baked." 
Ella was happy that she helped. They both finished stirring and put the cake in the oven. And when it was ready they both had a delicious piece of sweet cake!

Lily and Tom were two playful goats who lived in a valley with their mother. They liked to jump and run on the hills and eat the green grass. One day, they saw a big tent near the river. They were curious and wanted to see what was inside.
They ran to the tent and peeked through a hole. They saw a man and a woman who were cooking something on a fire. They smelled something yummy and their mouths watered. They heard the man say, "This soup will serve us well for dinner. It has carrots and potatoes and beans."
Lily and Tom wanted to taste the soup. They thought the man and the woman would not mind if they had a little sip. They waited until the man and the woman went to fetch some water from the river. Then they sneaked into the tent and found the pot of soup. They dipped their noses into the pot and slurped the soup.
But the soup was very hot and spicy. It burned their tongues and made them cough. They ran out of the tent, bleating and crying. The man and the woman heard the noise and came back. They saw the goats and the spilled soup and were angry.
"Hey, you naughty goats! You ruined our dinner! Go away and don't come back!" the man shouted.
Lily and Tom felt sorry and ashamed. They ran back to their mother and told her what they had done. Their mother scolded them and said, "You should not take what is not yours. You should respect other people's things. You should say sorry to the man and the woman and offer to help them."
Lily and Tom nodded and agreed. They went back to the tent and apologized to the man and the woman. They offered to help them clean the mess and find some more food. The man and the woman forgave them and thanked them. They shared some bread and cheese with them and invited them to stay for the night.
Lily and Tom learned their lesson and became friends with the man and the woman. They enjoyed the warm tent and the cozy fire. They slept well and dreamed of more adventures in the valley.

But Tommy did not listen. He wanted to do it by himself. He plugged the toaster into the wall and pushed the bread inside. He smiled and waited for the toast to pop out.
Suddenly, there was a loud bang and a flash of light. The toaster had exploded and sparks flew everywhere. Tommy screamed and fell off the chair. His mom ran to him and hugged him. She smelled something burning. She looked at Tommy's stomach and saw a big red mark. The toaster cord had touched his stomach and burned him.
"Tommy, Tommy, are you okay?" she asked, crying. She picked him up and ran to the phone. She called the doctor and told him what happened. She said they needed to go to the hospital right away.
Tommy was not okay. He was in a lot of pain and he was scared. He wished he had listened to his mom and not played with the toaster. He learned a hard lesson that day. He never tried to make toast by himself again.

"Let's whisper a secret to each other," she said. "But don't tell anyone else, okay?"

"What did you say?" he asked.
"I said I don't like you anymore," Lily said. "You are mean and boring and I don't want to be your friend."
Tom felt a big hurt in his heart. He dropped the microphone and ran away, crying. Lily laughed and picked up the microphone. She didn't care about Tom. She only wanted to play with the microphone.
But she didn't know that the microphone was not a toy. It was a real microphone that belonged to a man who worked in the park. He used it to talk to the people who came to see the animals and the flowers. He had left it on a bench while he went to get some water.
When he came back, he heard Lily's voice on the loudspeaker. He heard her say that she didn't like Tom and that he was mean and boring. He also heard Tom's cry and saw him run away. He was very angry and sad. He walked up to Lily and took the microphone from her.
"Hey, what are you doing?" Lily said. "Give it back!"
"No, I won't," the man said. "This is not a toy. This is my microphone. And you are a very bad girl. You hurt your friend's feelings with your mean words. You should be ashamed of yourself."
Lily felt scared and sorry. She wanted to say sorry to Tom and to the man, but she couldn't. The man took her by the hand and led her to the park office. He called her parents and told them what she had done. They came and picked her up. They were very angry and sad too. They scolded her and took away her toys. They said she had to be kind and nice to others, or she would have no friends.
Lily cried and cried. She wished she had never found the microphone. She wished she had never whispered that secret. She wished she had been kind to Tom. But it was too late. She had lost her best friend and her fun. She had a very bad day.

Lily and Ben wanted to play. They each had one dollar left. They looked at the prizes. There were dolls, cars, balls, and books. But there was one prize that they both wanted more than anything. It was a big, fluffy, rainbow unicorn. It was the most beautiful thing they had ever seen.

"Please, mister, can we have the unicorn instead?" Ben asked.
The man looked at them. He saw their sad faces and their hopeful eyes. He felt sorry for them. He smiled and said: "You know what, kids, you can have the unicorn. You tried very hard and you were very polite. You deserve a special prize."
Lily and Ben could not believe it. They were so happy. They thanked the man and hugged the unicorn. They shared it and played with it. They named it Sparkle. It was their favorite toy.

Lily liked ice cream very much. She liked to eat it on hot days, or when she was sad, or when she was happy. She liked all kinds of ice cream, but her favorite was chocolate. She liked to lick it from a cone, and feel it melt in her mouth.
One day, Lily went to the park with her mom. She saw a man with a cart, who had many cones and ice cream. She asked her mom if she could have one. Her mom said yes, and gave her some money. Lily ran to the man, and said, "Please, can I have a cone with chocolate ice cream?"
The man looked at Lily, and said, "No, you can't. I don't have any chocolate ice cream. I only have vanilla, and strawberry, and mint. You have to choose one of those, or go away."
Lily felt very sad, and very angry. She liked vanilla, and strawberry, and mint, but she wanted chocolate. She said, "But I want chocolate. Why don't you have chocolate? That's not fair."
The man said, "I don't care what you want. You can't have chocolate, because I don't have it. Stop being rude, and take what I have, or leave me alone."
Lily felt tears in her eyes. She thought the man was very rude, and very mean. She didn't want to take what he had, or leave him alone. She wanted to have chocolate ice cream, and make him sorry. She remembered what her mom had taught her, about being polite, and sharing, and saying sorry. But she also remembered what her dad had taught her, about standing up for herself, and not letting people bully her, and being brave.
She looked at the man, and said, "You are rude, and mean, and I don't like you. You should have chocolate ice cream, and you should share it, and you should say sorry. But you don't, and you won't, and you can't. So I will show you what I can do."
She took the money from her mom, and threw it at the man. Then she grabbed a cone, and scooped some vanilla ice cream, and some strawberry ice cream, and some mint ice cream. She made a big mess, and a big pile. Then she smashed the cone on the man's head, and ran away.
She ran to her mom, who was watching with a shocked face. She said, "Mom, I'm sorry, I was bad. But the man was rude, and mean, and he didn't have chocolate ice cream. I wanted to teach him a lesson."
Her mom hugged her, and said, "Lily, I love you, but you can't do that. You can't throw money, or grab cones, or smash ice cream. That's not polite, or nice, or brave. That's rude, and mean, and silly. You have to say sorry to the man, and to me, and to yourself. And you have to learn to accept what you have, and not what you want. Maybe next time, you will find chocolate ice cream, and you will be happy. But today, you have to be sorry, and sad, and sorry."
Lily nodded, and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I'm sorry, man. I'm sorry, me. I was rude, and mean, and silly. I will learn to accept what I have, and not what I want. But I still like chocolate ice cream, and I hope I will find it soon."
Her mom smiled, and said, "I still love you, Lily. And I still like chocolate ice cream, too. And I hope we will find it soon, too. But for now, let's go home, and have some water, and some cookies, and some hugs. And maybe, we will remember this day, and laugh, and not cry."
Lily smiled, and said, "OK, mom. Let's go home, and have some water, and some cookies, and some hugs. And maybe, we will remember this day, and laugh, and not cry. And maybe, we will find chocolate ice cream, and be happy, and not sad."
The end.

The gate had an old, heavy padlock on it that Daisy could not open. Suddenly, she heard a friendly voice coming up from behind her, “Would you like me to show you what is behind this gate?”
Daisy was startled and turned around to see a white rabbit with long ears and a long, leather tail. Daisy was happy to meet the rabbit, who introduced himself as Mr. Rabbit.
Mr. Rabbit explained, “If you follow me, I will lead you to a special place through the gate and you can discover what is around the bend”. 
Daisy followed the rabbit beyond the leather gate, not knowing what was to come. The path was quiet as the two friends walked along, until they came upon a wondrous field. 
Delighted, Daisy shouted for joy, for she had discovered the most beautiful garden she had ever seen. Daisy and Mr. Rabbit had plenty of fun exploring the garden together, until the sun set and it was time for Daisy to go home. 
Daisy thanked Mr. Rabbit for leading her to this special place and waved goodbye to him as she hopped away, content

Seeing his reaction, Jessica laughed. She then suggested that they forget the game, and share the arrow. She said that if Tim and his friends shared the arrow, everyone would get to enjoy it. 
Tim thought about it for a moment, then smiled and agreed. He realized that sharing was the best way to make everyone happy. 
From then on, Tim and his friends shared the arrow, always laughing and having a good time.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there lived a popular bunny named Bob. Bob had many friends because he was very nice. One day, Bob and his friends went to play hide and seek. Bob was very good at this game, so he always found his friends quickly.
"Ready or not, here I come!" shouted Bob. He looked behind a tree and found his friend, the squirrel. Then, he looked under a bush and found his friend, the mouse. Bob knew his last friend, the bird, was hiding in a high place. He looked up at the sky and saw a big tree. Bob thought the bird was hiding there.
Bob hopped to the big tree and started to climb. As he climbed, he felt something strange in his chest. He didn't know that it was his lung. When he reached the top, he saw his friend, the bird. "I found you!" said Bob. The bird smiled and said, "Good job, Bob! You are the best at this game!"
Bob was very happy. But then, he remembered the strange feeling in his chest. He told his friends about it. They all decided to go see the wise old owl for help. The owl listened to Bob's story and said, "Bob, you have discovered your lung. It helps you breathe when you climb and play."
Bob and his friends were amazed. They thanked the wise old owl and went back to play more games. Now, whenever Bob felt his lung, he knew it was helping him have fun with his friends. And they all lived happily ever after.

Joe replied, “Yes, this is my plan.”
The moral of the story is: sometimes it's best to stick to your plan. Joe was smart to listen to his mom and it was a good plan to only buy one type of gum. This made him feel better and much less fearful.

Mia smiled back and held the fork up in the air, beaming with pride. She had found the shiny, silver fork and that made her happy. The end.

The sound grew louder and louder, until one day, a little boy said, "It sounds like something is roaring!"
Each time the jeep ventured out, the roar grew louder and harsher. Everyone was scared and confused and did not know what the loud roaring was coming from.

Dan said, "What did you do that for, Joe?"
"I want to see what happens when I splash the flute," said Joe.
Suddenly, an ugly creature popped out of the water. It had green scales and yellow eyes. Joe and Dan were shocked.
The creature said, "I'm the guardian of the river. What were you doing, splashing things around in here?"
Joe said, "I was just playing with my flute."
The creature nodded and said, "Well, no more splashing around in here. I don't want to see any ugly creatures in the river."
Joe and Dan nodded and then quickly left. From then on, they made sure to not splash things around in the river.

The band began to play a gentle jazz tune. Jazz smiled and started to whisper the words of the song. She felt so happy and free. As the light faded, the band slowly stopped playing and Jazz thanked them with a smile before she went back inside.
