Ben and Lily were playing with their toy castle in the garden. They liked to pretend they were a king and a queen, and they had many knights and horses and dragons to protect them. They also had a big pair of scissors that they used to cut paper and make flags and banners for their castle.
One day, a new boy moved in next door. His name was Max, and he wanted to play with Ben and Lily. He knocked on the fence and said, "Hello, can I join you?"
Ben and Lily looked at each other and nodded. They liked to make new friends. They invited Max to come over and showed him their castle and their scissors. Max said, "Wow, this is a cool castle. Can I cut something with your scissors?"
Ben and Lily said, "Sure, but be careful. The scissors are sharp and they can hurt you. And don't cut our castle, please. We worked hard to make it."
Max said, "OK, I won't cut your castle. I'll cut something else." He looked around and saw a red pepper that Lily's mom had left on the table. He picked it up and said, "What about this? Can I cut this?"
Ben and Lily said, "No, don't cut that! That's a spicy pepper. It will make your mouth burn and your eyes water. You won't like it."
Max said, "I don't believe you. I like spicy things. I'll cut it and taste it. You'll see." He snipped the pepper with the scissors and put a piece in his mouth.
As soon as he bit the pepper, he felt a fire in his mouth. He spit it out and screamed, "Aaaah! This is too spicy! It hurts! It hurts!" He ran to the hose and sprayed water in his mouth, but it didn't help. He cried and cried and wished he had listened to Ben and Lily.
Ben and Lily felt sorry for Max. They ran to him and gave him some milk and bread. They said, "We're sorry, Max. We tried to warn you. The pepper is very spicy. It's not for kids. Are you OK?"
Max said, "I'm sorry, too. I was silly and rude. I should have listened to you. You were right. The pepper is very spicy. It's not for kids. Thank you for helping me. Can we still be friends?"
Ben and Lily said, "Of course we can. We're glad you're OK. Come on, let's play with our castle. But no more cutting peppers, OK?"
Max said, "OK, no more cutting peppers. Let's play with your castle. It's very cool. Can I be a knight?"
Ben and Lily said, "Sure, you can be a knight. We'll have a lot of fun."
And they did. They played with their castle and their scissors and their pepper, but they never cut it again. They learned their lesson. And they became good friends. The end.

One day, a boy named Tom went to the pond with his mom. He liked to look at the fish and the ducks and the bugs. He saw a frog sitting on a big leaf. He wanted to catch the frog and play with it.
"Mom, can I have the frog?" he asked.
"No, Tom, you can't have the frog. The frog is not a toy. The frog has a home and a family and he likes to be free. You have to be kind and humble and let the frog be," his mom said.
"But why, mom? I like the frog. He is green and he can jump and he can croak. He is fun," Tom said.
"Tom, you have to understand that the frog is not for you. He is a living thing and he has feelings and needs. He is not fun for you, he is scared and sad. He wants to stay in the pond and be with his friends. You have to respect the frog and leave him alone," his mom said.
Tom looked at the frog and he saw that the frog was not happy. He saw that the frog was shaking and hiding and trying to get away. He felt sorry for the frog and he realized that his mom was right. He did not want to hurt the frog or make him unhappy. He wanted to be a good and humble boy.
"OK, mom, I understand. I will not catch the frog. I will let him be. I will say sorry to the frog and I will wave goodbye," Tom said.
He went to the leaf and he said to the frog, "Sorry, frog, I did not mean to bother you. You are a nice frog and I hope you have a good day. Goodbye, frog." He waved his hand and he smiled.
The frog saw that Tom was kind and humble and he forgave him. He croaked and he waved his leg and he smiled too.
Tom and his mom walked away from the pond. They were happy and they learned something new. They understood that the frog was not a toy, but a friend.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play with round things. They have a ball, a hoop, and a wheel. They roll them, throw them, and spin them. They have fun.
One day, they see a big round thing in the park. It is shiny and red. It has a handle on top. They want to play with it. They run to it.
"Wow, what is this?" Tom asks.
"I don't know, but it looks fun. Let's lift it and see what it does," Mia says.
They try to lift it, but it is too heavy. They pull and push, but it does not move. They get tired and sad.
"Maybe we need help," Tom says.
"Maybe we can ask someone," Mia says.
They look around and see a friendly man. He is wearing a blue suit and a hat. He has a badge on his chest. He is walking towards them.
"Hello, kids. What are you doing?" he asks.
"We want to play with this round thing, but we can't lift it. Can you help us?" Tom asks.
The man smiles and shakes his head. He says, "I'm sorry, kids, but this is not a toy. This is a fire hydrant. It is for putting out fires. You can't play with it. It is dangerous."
"Dangerous? Why?" Mia asks.
"Because it has water inside. A lot of water. If you lift the handle, the water will come out very fast and very strong. It can hurt you and make a big mess. You don't want that, do you?" the man says.
Tom and Mia shake their heads. They say, "No, we don't."
The man says, "That's good. Now, why don't you go and play with your other round things? They are safer and more fun. And remember, never touch a fire hydrant, okay?"
Tom and Mia nod. They say, "Okay. Thank you, mister."
They run back to their ball, their hoop, and their wheel. They play with them and forget about the fire hydrant. They have fun.

You will be careful and respectful. You will be good."
Tom and Sue nod. They say, "We promise, sir. We will not play on the tree again. We will be careful and respectful. We will be good." They smile. They thank the park keeper. He gives them some limes. But they do not see the cook. The cook is walking with a big pot of soup. He is going to the picnic table. He does not see Tom and Mia. They do not see him. They go down the hill very fast. They hit the cook. The cook falls down. The pot of soup falls down. The soup is hot. It burns Tom and Mia. They scream. They cry. The cook is angry. He shouts. He says, "You are bad kids! Tom and Mia are sorry. They say, "We are sorry, cook. We did not see you. We did not mean to hurt you." But the cook does not listen. He takes their scooters. He says, "These are mine now. You can't have them back. You can't play with them anymore." He walks away with their scooters.
Tom and Mia are sad. They have no scooters. They have no fun. They have burns. They have a bad day. They wish they did not go down the hill. They wish they saw the cook. They wish they had different scooters.

Lily hated clowns. She hated their big red noses, their silly clothes, and their loud laughs. She hated how they made funny faces and threw pies at each other. She hated how they scared her with their balloons and tricks.
One day, Lily had to go to a birthday party. She did not want to go, but her mom said she had to. She said it would be fun and there would be cake and games. Lily hoped there would be no clowns.
But when she got to the party, she saw a big pink clown. He had a pink wig, a pink suit, and a pink bike. He smiled at Lily and said, "Hi, little girl! Do you want to see a magic trick?"
Lily shook her head and ran away. She hid behind a table and cried. She did not like the pink clown. She did not like magic tricks. She wanted to go home.
The pink clown saw Lily crying and felt sad. He did not want to make her cry. He wanted to make her happy. He walked over to her and said, "I'm sorry, little girl. I didn't mean to scare you. I'm a nice clown. I like to make people laugh. Do you want to be my friend?"
Lily looked at the pink clown. He did not look so scary anymore. He looked kind and sad. He had a big pink heart on his chest. Lily felt sorry for him. She said, "OK, I'll be your friend. But no magic tricks, OK?"
The pink clown nodded and smiled. He said, "OK, no magic tricks. How about a hug?"
Lily nodded and smiled. She gave the pink clown a hug. He gave her a hug back. He said, "Thank you, little girl. You made me happy."
Lily said, "You're welcome, pink clown. You made me happy, too."
They became friends and played together. Lily learned that clowns were not so bad. She learned that pink was not so bad. She learned that sometimes, things that you hate can become things that you love.

"We have new pedals!" Tim says.
"We have new pedals!" Sam says.

Then Sam saw a high mountain. He thought, "Maybe there is gold at the top!"

He shouted, "I find gold!" Everyone was so happy. Sam went home with a lot of gold.
The End.

The mechanic arrived and he was wearing blue overalls. He opened the hood of the car and rubbed his chin thoughtfully. He began to tinker with the engine and after a while the car roared into life.
Kate was so happy! She took the mechanic to the bakery and bought him a yummy cake to say thank you. He smiled and said it was the best reward he ever had.
Kate and the mechanic waved goodbye and Kate drove off happily in her car. She waved to the mechanic whenever she passed him and soon they were friends.

Once there was a boy named John who liked to make things out of wood. He had a big pile of original wood in his room. He had a saw and some nails, so he could make anything he wanted.

John was so proud of his chair. It looked better than any chair he had ever seen. He listed it in the window, and everyone who passed by noticed it. They all said it was the most beautiful chair they had ever seen.
John had made something special. He had taken one piece of original wood and made it into something amazing. And he was very proud of it.

Lily and Ben love to race. They race on their bikes, they race on their feet, they race on their sleds. They always have fun, but they also want to win. One day, they go to the beach with their mom and dad. They see a big boat that takes people to see whales. They want to go on the boat and race to see who can find a whale first.
Mom and dad buy tickets for the boat and they all get on. Lily and Ben run to the front of the boat and look at the water. They see many fish and birds, but no whales. They keep looking and looking, but they don't see any. They start to feel bored and sad. They want to see a whale and win the race.
Then, they hear a loud splash. They turn around and see a huge whale jumping out of the water. It is gray and white and has a big tail. It looks friendly and happy. Lily and Ben are amazed and excited. They both point at the whale and shout, "I see it, I see it, I win, I win!"
But the whale is not happy to see them. The whale thinks they are rude and noisy. The whale does not like to be pointed at and shouted at. The whale gets angry and decides to teach them a lesson. The whale swims closer to the boat and slaps its tail on the water. The water splashes all over the boat and makes everyone wet. Lily and Ben get scared and cry. They run to their mom and dad and hug them. They say they are sorry and they don't want to race anymore. They just want to go home.
The whale sees them crying and feels sorry for them. The whale knows they are just kids and they don't know better. The whale swims away and leaves them alone. The boat turns around and goes back to the shore. Lily and Ben learn their lesson. They learn to be quiet and respectful when they see animals. They learn that racing is not always fun and that sometimes it is better to share and enjoy. They also learn that whales are not friendly and that they should stay away from them. They never want to see a whale again. The end.

Tom and Mia were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big tree with many leaves. They wanted to climb the tree and see what was up there.
They took turns to go up the tree. Tom went first. He saw a bird nest with three eggs. He saw a squirrel with a nut. He saw a spider web with a shiny insect. He wanted to touch the insect, but the spider scared him. He said, "Mia, look at this insect! It is so pretty and shiny!"
Mia went up the tree. She saw the insect too. She liked it very much. She said, "Tom, can I have the insect? I want to keep it as a pet!"
Tom said, "No, Mia, it is mine! I saw it first!"
Mia said, "But I like it more! Please, Tom, give it to me!"
Tom and Mia started to fight. They pulled and pushed and shouted. The spider was angry. It bit Tom on his hand. Tom cried out loud. He let go of the insect. The insect flew away.
Mia said, "Tom, are you okay? I am sorry, I did not mean to hurt you."
Tom said, "Mia, I am sorry too. I should have shared with you. The insect is gone now. We were silly to fight over it."
Tom and Mia hugged each other. They climbed down the tree. They saw their mom waiting for them. She had a basket with snacks and juice. She said, "Are you hungry, my loves? Come and have some food. You look tired from playing."
Tom and Mia said, "Yes, mom, we are hungry. Thank you for the food. We love you, mom."
They ran to their mom. They ate and drank and told her about their adventure. They learned to yield and share and be kind. They had a happy day in the park.

Lila wanted to soar like a bird. She loved to watch them fly high in the sky, with their wings spread wide. She wished she had wings too, so she could join them and see the world from above.
One day, she saw a big plane in the air. It looked like a metal bird, but much louder and faster. She wondered who was inside, and where they were going. She ran to her mom and asked, "Mom, can we go on a plane someday?"
Mom smiled and hugged her. "Maybe, Lila. But planes are not for everyone. Some people are afraid of heights, or get sick on planes. And some people have to wear uniforms and work on planes, like pilots and flight attendants. They have to take care of the passengers and the plane, and follow many rules."
Lila thought about that. She did not like rules, or getting sick, or being afraid. But she still wanted to soar. She asked, "Mom, can I be a pilot when I grow up?"
Mom kissed her forehead. "You can be anything you want, Lila. But you have to work hard, and learn a lot, and be brave. Being a pilot is not easy. Sometimes, planes have problems, or bad weather, or emergencies. Then, the pilot has to be calm and smart, and try to fix the situation. Otherwise, the plane and the people on it could be in danger, and feel helpless."
Lila felt a shiver in her spine. She did not like danger, or feeling helpless. She imagined being on a plane that was falling, or on fire, or lost. She felt scared, and hugged her mom tighter. She said, "Mom, I changed my mind. I don't want to be a pilot anymore. I just want to be with you."
Mom smiled and rocked her gently. "That's okay, Lila. You don't have to be a pilot, if you don't want to. You can still soar in your dreams, or in your imagination, or with your toys. You can still watch the birds, and the planes, and enjoy their beauty. And you can always be with me, my sweet girl. I love you, Lila."
Lila felt warm and safe in her mom's arms. She said, "I love you too, Mom. Thank you for being my mom."
They cuddled for a while, and watched the sky together. Lila still wanted to soar, but she was happy where she was. She knew that her mom was the best person to soar with.

Lily was a little dog who loved to sing. She sang when she was happy, she sang when she was sad, she sang when she was bored. She sang to the birds, the flowers, the sun and the moon. She sang all day long.
One day, she found a big bone in the park. She was very happy and ran to it. She picked it up with her mouth and started to sing. She sang a song about the bone, how tasty it was, how lucky she was, how much she liked it.
But then, she heard a loud growl behind her. She turned around and saw a big dog, bigger than her, with sharp teeth and angry eyes. The big dog wanted the bone. He barked at Lily and said, "Give me the bone, or I will bite you!"
Lily was frightened. She did not want to give up the bone, but she did not want to be bitten either. She did not know what to do. She looked at the big dog and said, "Please, can we share the bone? I found it first, but you can have some too. I don't want to fight with you."
The big dog was surprised. He had never heard a dog sing before. He had never heard a dog ask to share before. He was used to taking what he wanted by force. He looked at Lily and said, "You sing? Why do you sing?"
Lily said, "I sing because I love to sing. Singing makes me happy. Singing makes everything better. Do you want to sing with me?"
The big dog was curious. He had never tried to sing before. He said, "How do you sing?"
Lily said, "It's easy. You just open your mouth and make a sound. Like this: woof, woof, woof!"
The big dog said, "Woof, woof, woof?"
Lily said, "Yes, that's it! Now, let's sing a song about the bone. Like this: woof, woof, woof, we have a bone, woof, woof, woof, we are not alone, woof, woof, woof, we can be friends, woof, woof, woof, until the end!"
The big dog said, "Woof, woof, woof, we have a bone, woof, woof, woof, we are not alone, woof, woof, woof, we can be friends, woof, woof, woof, until the end!"
Lily and the big dog sang together. They sang louder and louder, until everyone in the park heard them. They sang until they were tired and hungry. Then, they ate the bone together, and shared it equally. They became friends, and decided to sing every day. They were happy.

Anna said, "Maybe it belongs to a giant who lives in the woods. He was walking to the park to have a picnic, but he stepped on a thorn and it hurt his foot. He took off his boot and threw it away, but he forgot to take his sandwich with him."
Ben said, "Or maybe it belongs to a pirate who sailed to the park on his ship. He was looking for treasure, but he found a snake instead. He kicked the snake with his boot, but the snake bit his leg. He ran away and left his boot and his map behind."
Grandma listened to their stories and smiled. She said, "You have very good imaginations, my dears. But I think I know the real story of the boot. It belongs to Mr. Jones, the gardener. He works very hard to keep the park clean and beautiful. He has a pair of old boots that he wears when he mows the grass and digs the soil. He must have taken them off to rest his feet and forgot to put them back on. He will be looking for them soon."
Anna and Ben looked at the boot and nodded. They thought that was a nice story too. They decided to leave the boot where it was, so Mr. Jones could find it. They thanked grandma for taking them to the park and gave her a hug. They had a lot of fun and learned a lot of new words.

"Sorry, kids. You can't keep this. It is dangerous. You have to wash your hands now," she says.

They made loud noises as they lifted off the ground. They imagined they were zooming through the sky and seeing all kinds of wonders. They laughed and cheered as they reached the moon.
"Wow, look at that!" Lily said, pointing to a big crater. "Let's go explore!"
They got out of the rocket and jumped around. They felt very light and happy. They picked up some rocks and threw them in the air. They saw a flag and a footprint. They wondered who had been there before.
Suddenly, they heard a loud voice. It was Lily's mom. She was calling them from the park gate.
"Lily, Ben, time to go home! It's getting cold and dark!"
Lily and Ben looked at each other. They were upset. They didn't want to leave their rocket and their moon adventure. They wanted to stay and play some more.
"Can we have five more minutes, please?" Lily asked.
"No, you can't. It's too late. Come on, hurry up!" Lily's mom said.
Lily and Ben sighed. They got back into their rocket and pretended to land. They got out of the box and dragged it to the gate. They were sad and angry.
They passed by a fountain on the way. They saw some water spraying out of it. They had an idea.
"Let's freeze the fountain!" Ben whispered to Lily.
"How?" Lily asked.
"Watch this!" Ben said. He took a deep breath and blew as hard as he could at the fountain. He made a freezing sound.
Lily did the same. They both blew and blew until they ran out of air. They looked at the fountain. It was still spraying water.
They frowned. It didn't work. They felt silly.
They heard Lily's mom laughing. She had seen them trying to freeze the fountain.
"What are you doing, you silly geese?" she asked.
"We were trying to freeze the fountain, like astronauts!" Lily said.
"Astronauts don't freeze fountains, they explore space!" Lily's mom said.
"Well, we did that too!" Ben said.
"Really? Tell me all about it!" Lily's mom said.
Lily and Ben smiled. They forgot their upset feelings. They told Lily's mom all about their rocket and their moon adventure. They showed her their rocks and their flag. They made her laugh with their noises and their jumps.
Lily's mom hugged them and praised them for their imagination and creativity. She told them they were very clever and brave astronauts. She said they could play with their rocket again tomorrow, if they wanted.
Lily and Ben felt happy again. They thanked Lily's mom and said goodbye. They went home with their parents, holding their rocket and their rocks. They looked at the sky and saw the moon shining. They waved at it and smiled. They had a lot of fun today. They couldn't wait for tomorrow.

The frog happily said yes. But then, the sheep realized he didn’t know how to help the frog jump over a large rock in their path. The sheep tried to push the rock, but it was too heavy for him to move.
The sheep was now feeling very frustrated, because he wasn’t sure how to help the frog. After a few minutes of thinking, the sheep had an idea.
He decided to grab a bunch of wool and use it to cover the rock. This way, the frog could hop over the rock, while the sheep could pull it away. The wool worked perfectly, and the frog was able to hop right over the rock with ease.

Mommy and Jackie were excitedly packing their suitcases for a big trip to the other side of the world. Jackie asked what was in the thick envelope Mommy held in her hands.
"It's my passport so I can go on the big trip with you", Mommy said. "We will have a lot of fun!"
Jackie took out her own thin passport and compared it to Mommy's. "It's so thick!", she exclaimed with admiration.
On the day of the trip, Mommy and Jackie arrived at the airport. They saw the long lines of people waiting to board the long international flights. Mommy opened her thick passport to show the officer and Jackie did the same.
But suddenly the officer's face went from friendly to stern. Mommy's passport was no good. It had expired two months ago!
The moral of this story is that it's important to take care of important documents like passports or any other type of IDs. Always remember to check the expiration date!

One particularly curious little three-year-old was mesmerized by the hedge. Every morning he would go outside and watch the hedge blink. He wasn't sure why it was doing it- maybe it was magical? 
He thought about it a lot, but he just couldn't figure it out. After weeks of pondering, he finally decided to ask the hedge. He walked up to the hedge, closed his eyes and asked, "Why do you blink?" 
Suddenly, the hedge came to life and said, "To remind you to be brave, have faith and never give up. Blinking is my way of making sure you keep your spirit alive!" 
The little boy was amazed! He thanked the hedge and skipped away, feeling encouraged and inspired. From then on whenever he felt afraid or unsure, he would look at the blinking hedge and remember to keep going.

The little girl peered over the settle, wondering what was so special about it. Before she could go over there, her family called her to the their table. She reluctantly returned to their table and started to eat her dinner. 
As the meal went on, the little girl became more and more impatient. She wanted to know what was hidden behind that settle. Finally, when the meal was over, she ran to the settle, pushing it over. Ben liked to look for insects in the garden. He had a jar with holes in the lid, and he wanted to fill it with different kinds of insects. He liked to watch them crawl and fly and make noises.
One day, he saw a big, shiny insect on a flower. It had four wings and a long tail. It was green and blue and yellow. Ben thought it was the most beautiful insect he had ever seen. He wanted to catch it and put it in his jar.
He ran to the flower and reached out his hand. But before he could grab the insect, he heard a loud buzz and felt a sharp pain in his finger. He screamed and dropped the jar. The insect flew away.
"Ow, ow, ow!" Ben cried. He ran to his mom, who was sitting on the porch. She saw his finger and hugged him.
"What happened, Ben?" she asked.
"I tried to catch a pretty insect, but it stung me!" Ben sobbed.
"Oh, Ben, I'm sorry. That was a bee. Bees are not good insects to catch. They can hurt you. They make honey, but they also have stingers. You have to be careful around them."
She took him inside and put some ice on his finger. She gave him a cookie and a glass of milk. She kissed his finger and his cheek.
"Next time, I recommend you look for other insects, like butterflies or ladybugs. They are also pretty, but they don't sting. They are more available and friendly. Do you understand?"
Ben nodded. He felt better. He learned his lesson. He decided to leave the bees alone and look for other insects. He hoped he would find a butterfly or a ladybug soon. He still liked insects, but he was more careful now.

"I don't want to wear this coat!" Sara says. "It is ugly and itchy. I want to wear my pink dress."
"You can't wear your dress, Sara," Tom says. "It is too wet and muddy. You will get sick and dirty. And your dress is expensive. Mom will be mad."
"I don't care," Sara says. "I want to look pretty. You are silly and boring. You always wear the same coat and boots."
Sara runs to her room and puts on her dress. She sneaks out of the door and goes to the yard. She jumps in a puddle and laughs.
Tom follows her and sees her dress. He is shocked and angry. He runs to her and tries to pull her back.
"Stop, Sara, stop!" he says. "You are ruining your dress. Come inside. Mom will be here soon."
"Leave me alone, Tom!" Sara says. "You are mean and rude. I don't want to play with you. Go away."
They start to fight and push each other. They fall in the mud and get wet and dirty. They cry and scream.
Mom comes home and sees them. She is shocked and angry. She takes them inside and scolds them.
"What have you done, Sara and Tom?" she says. "You are both in trouble. You have to clean up and say sorry. And Sara, your dress is expensive. You have to pay for it with your allowance."
Sara and Tom feel bad and ashamed. They apologize to Mom and to each other. They hug and make up. They promise to listen to Mom and to wear the right clothes for the weather.

Tom and Anna liked to play music with their toys. Tom had a drum and Anna had a flute. They made sounds with their toys and tried to follow a rhythm. A rhythm is when you make sounds that go together and have a pattern.
One day, they decided to play music outside in the garden. They found a nice spot under a big tree and started to play. Tom banged his drum and Anna blew her flute. They had fun making their own rhythm.
But then, a big bird came and landed on the tree. The bird was very bossy. It did not like the music that Tom and Anna made. It started to squawk and screech very loudly. It wanted to stop them from playing.
"Shoo, shoo, go away!" Tom said to the bird. "We are playing music, you are making noise!"
"No, no, you go away!" the bird said to Tom. "You are making noise, I am singing!"
The bird and Tom argued and shouted. Anna did not like the noise. She wanted to play music with Tom. She had an idea. She took her flute and started to play a different rhythm. A rhythm that sounded like the bird's squawks and screeches.
The bird heard Anna's flute and stopped shouting. It was surprised and curious. It listened to Anna's rhythm and tried to copy it. It squawked and screeched along with Anna's flute.
Tom heard Anna's flute and the bird's squawks. He was surprised and curious too. He stopped banging his drum and listened to Anna's rhythm. He liked it. He took his drum and started to play a different rhythm. A rhythm that matched Anna's flute and the bird's squawks.
Anna, Tom and the bird played music together. They made a new rhythm. A rhythm that spread through the garden and made them happy. They were not bossy anymore. They were friends.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play with their toys. One day, they found a big box of stickers in their room. They were very happy and wanted to stick them everywhere.
"Look, Sam, I have a sticker of a lion. I will put it on the wall," Tim said.
"No, Tim, you can't do that. Mom will be mad. She said the wall is not for stickers. Only paper is for stickers," Sam said.
But Tim did not listen. He spread the stickers all over the wall, the door, the window, and the bed. He thought it looked very pretty.
"Tim, stop it! You are making a mess. Mom will see and she will put us in jail," Sam said.
"Jail? What is jail?" Tim asked.
"Jail is a bad place where you can't play or have fun. You have to stay in a small room with bars and no toys. Mom will send us there if we are naughty," Sam said.
Tim was scared. He did not want to go to jail. He wanted to play and have fun. He looked at the wall and saw how many stickers he had used. He felt sorry.
"Sam, I'm sorry. I did not know. How can we fix it?" Tim asked.
Sam thought for a moment. He had an idea.
"Maybe we can peel off the stickers and put them back in the box. Then we can clean the wall with a cloth and some water. Maybe Mom will not notice," Sam said.
Tim and Sam worked together to remove the stickers and clean the wall. It was hard work, but they did it. They put the box of stickers away and hoped Mom would not find out.
When Mom came home, she did not see anything wrong. She hugged Tim and Sam and said she was glad they had a good day. Tim and Sam smiled and hugged her back. They were glad too. They decided to be more careful with their stickers next time.

Ben was hungry. He wanted toast for breakfast. He asked his mom, "Can I have toast, please?"
Mom said, "Yes, you can. But first, you have to brush your teeth and wash your face. Then you can have toast."
Ben nodded. He went to the bathroom. He brushed his teeth and washed his face. He was a good boy.
But when he came back to the kitchen, he saw something strange. His toast was gone. There was only a plate with some crumbs. He looked around. He saw a trail of crumbs on the floor. He followed the trail. He wondered, "Who took my toast?"
He wandered into the living room. He saw his dog, Spot, on the couch. Spot had something in his mouth. It was Ben's toast. Spot was chewing it. It looked tough. Ben was angry. He said, "Spot, you bad dog! You took my toast! That was mine!"
Spot looked at Ben. He wagged his tail. He dropped the toast. He licked Ben's face. He wanted to play. He did not know he did something wrong.
Ben was still hungry. He did not want the toast anymore. It was dirty and tough. He went back to the kitchen. He asked his mom, "Can I have something else, please?"
Mom said, "Of course, you can. How about some cereal and milk?"
Ben said, "Yes, please. That sounds good."
Mom smiled. She gave Ben some cereal and milk. She said, "Next time, don't leave your toast on the table. Spot likes toast, too. He is a sneaky dog."
Ben said, "I know. I will be careful. I love Spot, but he is a naughty dog."
Mom said, "I love Spot, too. But he needs to learn some manners."
They laughed. They ate their breakfast. They were happy.

Tim and Mia were best friends. They liked to play outside in the park. One day, they saw a big kite in the sky. It was red and yellow and had a long tail.
"Wow, look at the kite!" Tim said. "It is so pretty and high!"
"Let's follow it!" Mia said. "Maybe we can find who is flying it!"
They ran after the kite, holding hands. They crossed the grass, the bridge, and the hill. They did not see anyone with a string or a stick.
"Where is the kite going?" Tim asked. "It is moving very fast!"
"Maybe it is free!" Mia said. "Maybe it does not need anyone to fly it!"
They followed the kite until they reached a big tree. The kite got stuck on a branch. It could not fly anymore.
"Oh no, the kite is trapped!" Tim said. "We have to help it!"
They looked for a way to climb the tree. But the tree was too tall and the branch was too far. They could not reach the kite.
"Maybe we can ask someone for help!" Mia said. "Maybe someone has a ladder or a stick!"
They looked around, but they did not see anyone. They felt sad and sorry for the kite.
"Hello, children!" a voice said. "Do you need some help?"
They turned around and saw an old man. He had a kind face and a humble smile. He was holding a long stick.
"Are you the one who is flying the kite?" Tim asked.
"No, I am not," the old man said. "But I saw you following it. It is a very nice kite. Do you want to get it down?"
"Yes, please!" Mia said. "We want to free the kite!"
The old man nodded. He walked to the tree and used his stick to poke the kite. The kite came loose and fell to the ground. Tim and Mia ran to pick it up.
"Thank you, thank you!" they said to the old man. "You are very kind and helpful!"
The old man smiled. "You are very welcome," he said. "You are very brave and curious. You can keep the kite if you want. Maybe it will fly again with you."

"Give me the potato!" Tom says.
"No, it is mine!" Sue says.
They pull and tug. They quarrel and shout. They are not happy.
Mom hears them. She comes to the garden. She sees the potato.
"What are you doing?" Mom asks.
"We found a potato. We both want it." Tom and Sue say.
Mom smiles. She has an idea.
"Why don't you share the potato?" Mom says. "You can wash it and cut it. Then we can cook it and eat it together. It will be yummy."
Tom and Sue think. They like yummy food. They do not like to quarrel.
"OK, Mom. We will share the potato." Tom and Sue say.
They let go of the potato. They hug and say sorry. They are friends again.
They wash the potato and cut it. Mom cooks it and makes a salad. They sit at the table and eat. They talk and laugh. They are happy.
The garden is peaceful. The potato is gone. But Tom and Sue have something better. They have each other.

Tom and Sam were playing in the garden. They liked to look for bugs and animals. They saw a cricket on a leaf. It was green and shiny.
"Look, a cricket!" Tom said. "I want to catch it!"
He reached out his hand to grab the cricket. But Sam stopped him.
"No, Tom, don't!" Sam said. "Cricket is dangerous. It can slap you with its legs. It can hurt you."
Tom did not listen to Sam. He thought Sam was silly. He wanted to touch the cricket. He moved his hand closer to the leaf.
The cricket saw Tom's hand. It did not like Tom. It felt scared. It jumped off the leaf and slapped Tom's hand with its legs. Tom felt a sharp pain. He cried out loud.
"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom said. "The cricket slapped me! It slapped me!"
Sam ran to Tom. He hugged him and said sorry.
"I told you, Tom, cricket is dangerous," Sam said. "You should listen to me. I am your big brother. I know things."
Tom nodded. He was sorry too. He learned his lesson. He did not want to touch cricket again. He wanted to play with Sam. They went to find other bugs and animals. They had fun in the garden.

Sara likes to write. She writes with her crayons on paper. She writes her name, and the names of her toys, and the things she sees. She writes big and small, and in many colors.
One day, she writes a story about a powerful dragon. The dragon is very big and strong. He can fly and breathe fire. He is the king of the sky and the land. He is very happy and kind. Sara likes her story. She shows it to her mom.
"Wow, Sara, this is a great story!" her mom says. "You are very good at writing. Where did you get the idea for the dragon?"
"I saw him in my dream," Sara says. "He was my friend. He told me his name is Rolo."
"That's a nice name," her mom says. "Do you want to keep your story, or do you want to throw it in the bin?"
"I want to keep it," Sara says. "I want to read it again and again. And maybe Rolo will come back in my dream."
"Okay, then," her mom says. "You can put it in your drawer, or on your wall, or wherever you like. But remember to clean up your crayons and paper, okay?"
"Okay, mom," Sara says. She puts her story in her drawer, and puts her crayons and paper in a box. She is very proud of her writing. She hopes Rolo will visit her again.

Lily and Max were playing in the park. They liked to slide, swing and run. But Max was not careful. He tripped on a rock and fell down. He hurt his knee and it was bleeding.
"Ow, ow, ow!" Max cried. "It hurts!"
Lily ran to him and hugged him. She saw his knee and said, "You need a bandage. A bandage will make it better."
She looked around and saw a lady with a bag. She ran to her and asked, "Please, can you help? My friend needs a bandage. He has a boo-boo."
The lady smiled and said, "Of course, I can help. I have some bandages in my bag. What color do you want?"
Lily looked at Max and said, "What color do you want, Max?"
Max thought for a moment and said, "I want green. Green is my favorite color."
The lady nodded and said, "Okay, here is a green bandage. Let me put it on your knee. There, does it feel better?"
Max looked at his knee and saw the green bandage. He smiled and said, "Yes, it feels better. Thank you, lady. And thank you, Lily. You are a good friend."
Lily smiled and said, "You are welcome, Max. I am glad you are okay. Do you want to play some more?"
Max nodded and said, "Yes, I want to play some more. But let's be careful. I don't want another boo-boo."
They hugged the lady and said goodbye. Then they went back to the playground and played some more. They had fun and they were happy.

Tom and Mia like to play at the park. They like to slide, swing and climb on the structure. The structure is big and has many colors. Tom and Mia have fun on the structure.
One day, a new boy comes to the park. His name is Sam. He has a big bike and a loud voice. He sees Tom and Mia on the structure. He wants to play too. But he does not ask nicely. He says, "Move! This is my structure now!"
Tom and Mia are scared and sad. They do not want to leave the structure. They like to play there. They say, "No, this is our structure. We were here first. You can play with us, but you have to share."
Sam does not like to share. He says, "No, I do not want to share. I want the whole structure for myself. You have to go away. Or I will push you!"
Tom and Mia do not know what to do. They do not want to fight with Sam. They do not want to get hurt. They look for help. They see a lady on a bench. She is reading a book. She has a modest dress and a kind smile. She is Tom and Mia's teacher. They run to her and tell her what happened.
The teacher listens to Tom and Mia. She is not happy with Sam. She says, "That is not nice, Sam. You cannot take the structure from Tom and Mia. You have to be polite and respectful. You have to ask if you can join them. And you have to share the structure with them. That is how you make friends and play well."
Sam feels ashamed. He knows he was wrong. He says, "I am sorry, Tom and Mia. I was rude and mean. Can I play with you on the structure? I will share and be nice."
Tom and Mia are glad. They say, "Yes, you can play with us. We will share and be nice too."
The teacher smiles. She says, "That is good, Sam. I am proud of you. Now you can all play together and have fun on the structure."
Tom, Mia and Sam go back to the structure. They slide, swing and climb. They laugh and talk. They have fun on the structure. They are friends.

Lily and Ben are playing with their toy printer. They like to print pictures of animals and cars and flowers. Lily is very bossy. She tells Ben what to print and how to print it.
"Print a big lion, Ben. Lions are my favorite. Make it roar!" Lily says.
Ben does not like lions. He likes elephants. He wants to print an elephant. But he is afraid of Lily. She is bigger than him and louder than him. He prints a lion.
"Good, Ben. Now print a salad. Salads are healthy. We can pretend to eat it." Lily says.
Ben does not like salads. He likes pizza. He wants to print a pizza. But he is afraid of Lily. She is stronger than him and faster than him. He prints a salad.
"Good, Ben. Now print a crown. I am the queen. You are my servant. You have to do what I say." Lily says.
Ben does not like crowns. He likes hats. He wants to print a hat. But he is afraid of Lily. She is smarter than him and prettier than him. He prints a crown.
Lily puts the crown on her head. She holds the lion and the salad. She smiles. She is happy. She thinks she is the best.
Ben is sad. He does not have any pictures he likes. He does not have any fun. He thinks he is the worst.
Then, Mom comes in. She sees the pictures. She sees Lily and Ben.
"What are you doing, kids?" Mom asks.
"We are playing with the printer. I am the queen. Ben is my servant." Lily says.
"Is that so? And do you like being the queen, Lily?" Mom asks.
"Yes, I do. I am very bossy. I tell Ben what to print and how to print it." Lily says.
"And do you like being the servant, Ben?" Mom asks.
"No, I don't. I am very sad. I don't get to print what I want and how I want it." Ben says.
Mom frowns. She does not like what she hears. She does not like bossy queens and sad servants. She has an idea.
"How about we switch roles, kids? Lily, you can be the servant. Ben, you can be the king. You can print what you want and how you want it. And you have to be nice to each other. OK?" Mom says.
Lily and Ben look at each other. They are surprised. They are curious. They nod.
"OK, Mom." They say.
Mom smiles. She gives them a hug. She leaves them to play.
Lily and Ben switch roles. Lily gives Ben the crown. Ben gives Lily the lion and the salad. They start to print new pictures. They print elephants and pizzas and hats. They print stars and hearts and rainbows. They print what they want and how they want it. They share and take turns. They say please and thank you. They laugh and smile. They are happy. They think they are the best.

Kitty got jealous and stopped eating her popcorn. She didn't want to watch Lucy show off her swimming skills. But then Lucy saw Kitty and asked if she wanted to join them. They all splashed around in the pool and had so much fun! 
Kitty was so happy that Lucy asked her to swim. She shared her popcorn with Lucy and Jake and they all laughed and smiled. From that day on, all three of them were the best of friends and went swimming and ate popcorn together. The end.

Once upon a time there was a naughty goat who wanted to be famous. He wanted to put a big billboard up in the middle of the town, but he didn't know how to do it.
So he asked the strong bull who lived next door. The bull said he had a plan, and it would make the goat famous. The plan was to pull the billboard with a rope.
The goat was excited. He tried to pull the billboard all by himself, but it was too heavy. So he asked all the tiny birds for help.
The tiny birds were jealous, but they agreed and flew from tree to tree, until the billboard was in the middle of the town. All the animals cheered, and the goat had become famous! He had succeeded!

Mandy had a pink dog. She loved it very much. She took it outside to play. The dog was so happy, it wagged its tail and bit on a stick. Mandy laughed and threw the stick again. The dog bit it and ran like it was flying.
Mandy was so proud of her dog. But then it saw a rabbit and decided to give chase. Mandy yelled "stop!" But the dog kept running. It chased the rabbit all the way to a tip.
The tip was full of muddy puddles. The dog ran so fast it splashed the mud up and made a big mess. Mandy laughed and called her dog back. She held the tip of the stick so the dog could bite it. Her pink dog was happy again.

Once upon a time there was a child who was very scared. She had a big exam and was so nervous she was shaking. The exam was made of thin paper, so the child was worried that she would not be able to do it properly.
Suddenly, a friendly bird flew in through the window and sat on her desk. It began to talk to her, in a gentle, comforting voice. It said, "Don't worry. You can do it! Just take a deep breath and take your time, one step at a time."
The child was so relieved. With the bird's help, she took the thin exam paper, slowly read every question, and slowly but surely she filled in her answers.
Finally, it was time to hand it in. The child nervously handed it to the teacher, and the teacher smiled. She had done her best, and it was enough! She felt so proud.
As the bird flew out of the window and away, the child thanked it silently. Then, with a big smile on her face, she confidently shook the teacher’s hand and said goodbye.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Jack. One day, Jack was playing in his garden and he had been very careful. Suddenly, something caught his ear. It was a lot of clapping. He looked around and saw that it was coming from the nearby park.
Curious, Jack went to have a look. When he arrived, he saw a lot of people applauding. Then he saw, to his surprise, that it was a clown. The clown was making everyone laugh and they were all enjoying it. Jack was very happy and started clapping too.
Everyone was very happy, even Jack's ear. He couldn't help but laugh and applaud. After the show was over, Jack thanked the clown. The clown smiled and said he was glad to make Jack smile.
The next day, Jack wanted to show the clown how grateful he was. He told his dad he wanted to make the clown a present. They went to the park and the clown was there again. But this time he was being careless.
Jack quickly ran to help the clown. He held up the clown's hat and the clown was so thankful. He put his hat back on and hugged Jack. Everyone clapped and cheered for Jack and the clown. They all knew that Jack had been very brave.

John was out in the backyard playing. He saw a funny looking insect and he laughed. He tried to catch the insect but it flew away. John became confused. He walked around the garden, looking for the insect. He heard a chuckle coming from the bushes. Suddenly, an insect popped out and flew into the air. It was the same funny looking insect from before! John laughed and jumped around the garden, trying to catch the insect. The insect was too fast though, and soon it was gone. John was confused but he was also filled with joy for the fun game he just played with the silly insect.

Once upon a time, there was a green vehicle. Every day it would ask an important question. But no one ever seemed to answer.
One day, a 3 year old heard about the question. He was very curious and decided to answer it. He was so brave!
The 3 year old walked up to the vehicle and confidently said: "I can answer your question!" 
The vehicle was so surprised! It was expecting an adult to answer, not a little boy. But the boy was brave and insisted that he could answer.
The vehicle finally asked the question, "What do you like to do most in the world?"
The 3 year old thought for a minute and then answered, "I like to play with my friends and laugh!"
The vehicle was so pleased with the answer. It thanked the 3 year old and said he was the bravest person around!
The 3 year old went off with a big smile on his face, proud that he had answered the question. He would never forget this special moment.

Once upon a time, there was a package. It was a special package full of surprises. One day, the package started to increase. It got bigger and bigger as it filled with more and more stuff.
At first, the package was very happy. The things inside were sweet and nice. But then one day, something sour arrived. It made the package sad. The sour was so strong that it made the package worry.
The package didn't know what to do. The sourness was increasing, and it was scared. But then one day, it felt something inside it. It was small, but happy. It couldn't be sour!
The package realized it was a smile. The package was excited and happy. The smile made the sour go away.
The package was happy again, and the smile stayed with it always. No matter what, it always increased the package's happiness.

Once upon a time, there was a thin rhinoceros. He loved going for walks in the park and taking in the sights. One day, while wandering, he spotted something special. From afar, he could see a shiny, sparkly rock. He was so surprised at the sight, he just had to take a closer look!
So, he trudged over, his feet clamoring over the soft grass. When he was close enough, he stopped and gazed at the stone. It was beautiful, with swirls of green and blues. He wanted it to be his, so he carefully picked it up.
He stared at it for a few moments more, then shuffled away, admiring his sparkling new treasure. He smiled the whole way home, giddy with excitement. He was so happy to have found such an amazing thing just for him!

Once there was a little girl named Sarah. She was three years old and loved to explore the world around her. One day, Sarah was playing in the garden when she heard a strange noise. She quickly ran to see what was going on. 
As she got closer, she saw the source of the noise. It was a dog, digging a big hole in the ground. Sarah's mind was a bit confused. She was so curious about why the dog was making all that noise. 
 
Sarah decided to ask the dog what he was doing. But when she got nearer, the dog ran away. She noticed that the dog had dug up a lot of dirt, making everything very dirty. Sarah looked around, trying to find the dog. 
Suddenly, she heard the same noise from before. Sarah looked around and noticed the dog was still digging the same hole. She thought it was so funny that the dog wanted to mind its own business and create a big mess. 
Sarah smiled, and decided to help the dog clean up all the dirt. She threw all the dirt back in the hole and patted the dog on the head. She was so happy to have made a new friend. After that, Sarah and the dog became best buddies!
